# Motion Doctrine (Gateway)

Read this before composing any animation. It decides WHAT happens at every seam and how
every scene performs; the technique skills implement it. These rules supersede generic /
upstream motion guidance. The failure this prevents: scenes authored in isolation — the
eye's momentum dies at every cut, and scenes wobble in place between entry and exit.

## Route map

| Decision (this skill)                              | Implementation skill                                                                              |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Seam transition choice + parameters + code         | `cut-the-curve` §1–5 (the catalog)                                                                |
| Text / element entry cascades                      | `cut-the-curve` §6 (waterfall entry)                                                              |
| In-scene group repositioning (no cut)              | `cut-the-curve` §7 (nudge curve)                                                                  |
| Cursor-led action / scene kickoff / morph ignition | `oversized-cursor`                                                                                |
| Seam render mechanics / white-flash guard          | `seam-craft`                                                                                      |
| Product-launch / explainer / caption work          | overlays `text-beat-economics`, `brand-faithful`, `captions-overlay` on top of the upstream skill |

Authoring order: **vector ledger (`ledger.json`) → STAMP the master seams from it
(`scripts/seam-stamp.mjs --ledger ledger.json --write index.html`) → sustained-motion
route per phase → carriers and causes → build comps → VERIFY (`scripts/seam-gate.mjs`).**
Hand-author only Tier-A morphs/match-cuts; stamped seams pass the gate by construction.

---

# Part 1 — The Seam Law

## The Vector Law

> How Scene A exits determines how Scene B enters: same axis, same direction, matched
> speed, cut mid-motion on both sides.

1. **Axis** — x stays x, y stays y, Z stays Z. Never trade axes across a cut.
2. **Direction** — never mirror. On Z, direction = the SIGN of scale change: growing =
   push (camera forward), shrinking = pull (camera back). A receding exit answered by a
   grow-from-small entry is a mirrored vector — the most common violation, because
   grow-from-small is the default element entrance.
3. **Speed** — entry initial velocity ≈ exit final velocity, via mirrored eases (exit
   `power4.in` + entry `power4.out`, same distance and duration; the incoming side picks
   up ≥50% through the notional path). Mechanics in `cut-the-curve`.
4. **Phase** — the cut lands mid-motion on BOTH sides. Settling to rest before the cut,
   or starting from rest after it, is a dead beat.

## The Current

Every film picks ONE dominant direction (house default: LEFT). Every ordinary seam uses
it. Other vectors are RESERVED — spending one means something:

| Vector                    | Meaning                                                         |
| ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The current (LEFT)        | "next beat" — neutral forward progress                          |
| Upward                    | elevation — a conclusion or reveal rises above what came before |
| Z forward (zoom-through)  | pushing deeper into the same thought                            |
| Z backward (inverse zoom) | ARRIVAL — something bigger lands                                |
| Scale-burst (explode out) | leaving a world — a surface blasts past camera                  |

- Never run consecutive seams in opposing directions — ping-pong reads as an error.
- A direction change needs a visible cause (click / bounce / impact) or a chapter boundary.

## The Vector Ledger

Write it before authoring any master timeline — as **`ledger.json` at the project root**
(schema: `references/seam-gate.md`). One row per seam: cut time, exit and entry vectors
(axis + signed direction; Z rows carry the scale sign), selectors, technique. Exit and
entry must match; if a row mismatches, fix the plan, not the easing. The verifier checks
row consistency statically before any runtime sampling.

## Carriers

The eye follows objects, not abstractions. The strongest seams hand a concrete carrier
across the cut at matched position AND velocity: a cursor mid-path, a container that
shrinks/docks into the next layout, a mark that flies into its exact slot, the word group
of a waterfall cut. With no natural carrier, the scene heroes carry it (partial travel +
early fade, entry mid-flight). Never a crossfade — it has no carrier at all.

## Causal Motion

Chain motion so each move is visibly launched by the last: click → squash → release
spring → flight → impact → recoil → reveal.

- Effects start ON the causing frame — same timeline position, never "shortly after."
- Reactions scale with implied mass: big elements rebound slower, small ones snap.
- A force is a license to change direction; an uncaused flip is a ping-pong.

## The Seam Gate (build gate — run the verifier, exit 0 or the seam is not done)

```bash
node <SKILL_DIR>/scripts/seam-stamp.mjs --ledger ledger.json --write index.html  # generate
node <SKILL_DIR>/scripts/seam-gate.mjs  verify --ledger ledger.json --project .  # verify
```

The script (usage + ledger schema: `references/seam-gate.md`) numerically enforces, per
seam: ledger-row consistency, exit still moving at the cut, entry mid-flight (never from
rest), measured direction = ledger direction, entry/exit speed match (WARN), **zero
overlap** (one side visible per frame — the cut is not a dissolve), the **Z sign** rule
(d(scale)/dt same sign both sides; the incoming scene's own entrances are scanned for
sign-fighting), and carrier rect continuity with ancestor scale included. Use
`seam-gate.mjs probe --t <cut>` to find each seam's true carrier selectors when authoring
the ledger.

Rules the script cannot check — still yours:

1. **Edits re-open the seam.** Any change to a scene's first/last ~1s (including
   re-timing to new VO) invalidates that boundary's audit — re-run the verifier.
2. **Audio is the clock.** Re-time scenes to the VO's real word timestamps; never rush a
   read to fit a slot. A VO regen re-opens its seams.
3. **Clip-gating gotcha** (the usual cause of a zero-overlap FAIL): a clip whose
   `data-start` precedes its entry tween is un-hidden at its initial opacity — set
   initial `autoAlpha: 0` AND `data-start` = the cut time, never earlier.

---

# Part 2 — Performance (the scene keeps performing)

## No idle wobble

Idle sine loops (breathe, float, drift, glow pulse) are BANNED as sustained motion — they
read as "the video is waiting." A scene that finishes entering with seconds left is a
planning bug: add story, not wobble. Every phase between entry and exit is owned by one
of these routes (name the route in the plan):

| Route                  | What it is                                                                                                             |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Staged reveals**     | Hold content back; pay it off on narration beats — the frame keeps gaining information (default for ≥2 content groups) |
| **Camera with intent** | A mapped scale+pan path: establish wide → travel → arrive on the subject                                               |
| **Sequenced UI life**  | The product behaves over time: progress advances, highlights step, counts tick                                         |
| **Animated sequences** | Elements act out a beat: a card files into a stack, an item gets dragged, a result assembles                           |
| **Cursor-led action**  | An oversized cursor walks the eye to a trigger; its CLICK ignites the next beat (`oversized-cursor`)                   |

Test: pause at any second — something meaningful must be mid-flight (a reveal landing,
the camera traveling, the UI doing what the narration says).

## Stillness before climax

Schedule a **0.3–0.75s pause** between the major action and its result — the dramatic
comma. A scene that jumps straight from action to result loses it.

## Timing intents

- Single entry ≤ ~800ms; longer buildup = multi-element stagger, not one slow element.
- Exit ≈ 75% of entry. Exception: cut-the-curve inverts this (entry ~127% of exit).
- Total stagger ≤ 500ms; with 8+ elements, tighten per-item delay or stagger the first few.
- Forbidden eases: `bounce.out` / `elastic.out`. Entry overshoot `back.out(1.4–1.7)` is fine.
- Similar elements share one ease+duration intent — never a unique pair per element.

## Transition vocabulary

Use only 2–3 inter-scene transitions per film and repeat them; the default boundary is
**cut-the-curve in the current's direction**. Hand-written shared-element morphs
(`intent: morph`) don't count against the budget.

---

## Anti-Patterns

| Don't                                                                      | Instead                                            |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| Author each scene's entrance in isolation                                  | Write the vector ledger first                      |
| Crossfade between scenes                                                   | Cut-the-curve in the current's direction           |
| Exit completes, THEN the scene changes                                     | Cut mid-motion on both sides                       |
| Entry starts from rest after a cut                                         | Enter ≥50% through the notional path               |
| Inverse-zoom exit → grow-from-small entry (or push → oversized retraction) | Match the scale-velocity sign (Seam Gate 7)        |
| Incoming scene's own pop-in intro under a Z-seam handoff                   | Hold its opening frame composed, or match the sign |
| Idle wobble / breathe / float to fill time                                 | Assign a sustained-motion route; or add story      |
| Direction flip without a cause                                             | Spend a force, or keep the current                 |
| Reserved vectors used as variety                                           | Default to the current; spend them on meaning      |
| Reaction a few frames after its cause                                      | Same-frame ignition                                |
| Action jumps straight to result                                            | Schedule stillness-before-climax (0.3–0.75s)       |

# Oversized Cursor — the eye-carrier

A deliberately oversized macOS-style pointer that travels the frame as a _visible
protagonist_: it enters from off-screen, walks the viewer's eye to the next point of
interest, clicks to cause the next thing that happens, and leaves. Production-proven
across multiple launch films.

**Why it exists.** Big cursor movement is one of the cheapest high-yield motion sources
in a launch video: one element, transform-only tweens, and it (1) brings the eye across
the screen on scenes that would otherwise read as dead, (2) gives causal ignition to
morphs/transitions ("the click did that"), and (3) segments the eye out of a stale
state when kicking off a new scene or a complex animation sequence. Bigger is better —
an actual-size cursor disappears at video scale.

## Size & look (house convention)

- **Full-frame scenes: `7cqw`** (≈134px at 1920). In-mock / small-frame variants:
  `4.6–5.5cqw`. Never smaller.
- One SVG arrow geometry everywhere. Two proven fills — white body + black stroke, or
  black body (`#1c1c1c`) + white stroke (1.4px). Pick per scene contrast, keep it
  constant per film.
- **Brand-motif cursors (the power play).** The macOS arrow is the DEFAULT, not a
  mandate. When the subject brand has a recognizable cursor identity — a collaborative
  design tool's colored multiplayer arrow with a name tag (Figma-style), a creative
  suite's precision crosshair, a distinctive product pointer — use THAT cursor instead:
  instantly legible brand language for anyone who knows the product. Same laws apply
  unchanged (oversized scale, physical entry/exit, tip-targeting, click-ignition), and
  a name-tag variant travels as one rigid unit (tag trailing the arrow). Reach for it
  only when the motif is genuinely referenceable; a cursor nobody recognizes is just a
  weird arrow — default back to macOS.
- `filter: drop-shadow(0 4px 6px rgba(0,0,0,.3))`, `pointer-events: none`,
  `z-index` above all scene content, `will-change: transform`.

```css
#root .cursor {
  position: absolute;
  left: 48%;
  top: 115%; /* off-screen below — the resting pose IS off-screen */
  width: 7cqw;
  height: 7cqw;
  z-index: 20;
  filter: drop-shadow(0 4px 6px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.3));
  pointer-events: none;
  will-change: transform;
}
```

## Entry law — physical, never revealed

The cursor **always enters from off-screen** (canonical: from below, `top:115–120%`)
and travels to its first target in one decelerating glide. It must _feel like it
entered the room_. Never opacity-fade it in at a resting position, never mask-reveal
it — that reads as a glitch (a real, repeatedly observed failure mode).

- Default path: **straight up the y-axis** to the target — no fragmented diagonals.
  A diagonal is fine when it IS the story (entering toward an off-axis target), but it
  is one continuous vector either way.
- `duration: 0.4–0.92s`, `ease: power3.out`, `immediateRender: false` on the fromTo.

```js
tl.fromTo(
  cursor,
  { left: "48.6%", top: "115%" },
  { left: "48.6%", top: "55%", duration: 0.85, ease: "power3.out", immediateRender: false },
  0.25,
);
```

## Tip-targeting & the click tap

The hot-spot is the arrow TIP, not the box center. Land the **tip** on the target's
center, and pivot all press scaling on the tip: `transformOrigin: '21% 14%'` (for the
house arrow path in a 24-unit viewBox).

Click = asymmetric compress/expand (1:2 ratio reads as a real tap):

```js
tl.to(cursor, { scale: 0.84, duration: 0.1, ease: "power2.in", transformOrigin: "21% 14%" }, t);
tl.to(
  cursor,
  { scale: 1, duration: 0.22, ease: "power2.out", transformOrigin: "21% 14%" },
  t + 0.1,
);
```

**The target's reaction is a separate, parallel tween** (button: `scale: 0.94` + press
color/shadow, starting at the same `t`). Cursor-only taps (e.g. focusing a text input)
get NO target reaction. Pair with `cursor-click-ripple` / `press-release-spring` for
the target side.

## The click IGNITES the next beat

Never let a morph, typing run, window transform, or scene-defining animation simply
_start_. Park the cursor on the trigger and let the click cause it, same-frame:

- click ▸ menu/submenu cascade, toggle flip
- click ▸ typing kickoff into an input
- click ▸ composer morph-down / window shrink
- click ▸ logo ignition / flight launch
- click ▸ play-state flip + UI-life wake in a product mock

During long beats it doesn't own (typing, narration), the cursor **drifts aside**
(0.5–0.9s, `power2.out`) — never sits frozen on top of the action, never wobbles idly.

## Exit law & cross-scene handoff

Two sanctioned exits — both physical, **never an opacity fade in place**:

1. **Leave the frame**: accelerate off the nearest edge with `power2.in`
   (`left:'118%'`, `left:'-12%'`, or `top:'116%'`), 0.5–0.7s.
2. **Cut-the-curve handoff**: in the final ~0.3s before a hard cut, the cursor starts
   accelerating (`power2.in`) toward the NEXT scene's first click point, covering the
   first ~1/3 of that path; the next composition `gsap.set`s the cursor at the
   handoff pose and continues with `power2.out` at matched velocity. The cursor itself
   becomes the carrier element that stitches the seam:

```js
// scene A, last 0.3s — start the journey:
tl.to(cursor, { left: "40.7%", top: "63.7%", duration: 0.3, ease: "power2.in" }, CUT - 0.3);
// scene B, t=0 — finish it at matched velocity:
gsap.set(cursorB, { left: "40.7%", top: "63.7%" });
tl.to(cursorB, { left: "22%", top: "45%", duration: 0.6, ease: "power2.out" }, 0);
```

## Checklist

- [ ] ≥ 7cqw full-frame (4.6–5.5cqw inside a mock) — when unsure, bigger
- [ ] enters from off-screen on one continuous vector (no fade/mask reveal)
- [ ] tip lands on the target center; press pivots on `transformOrigin: '21% 14%'`
- [ ] every click causes something, same-frame
- [ ] drifts aside during beats it doesn't own; zero idle wobble
- [ ] exits physically (off-frame or cut-the-curve handoff) — no fade-in-place

# Seam Craft — render prerequisites for scene-to-scene transitions

This is the **render-correctness doctrine** for PLV scene-to-scene seams: the
prerequisites and master-timeline mechanics that make any transition composite
correctly, independent of which specific transition is chosen. The per-transition
catalog (crossfade, push-slide, zoom-through, cut-the-curve, …) lives in the
transition registry — this page is the doctrine that sits underneath all of them.

The transitions this doctrine governs are **Tier-B-ready**: pure transform / opacity /
filter on the two scene **clip wrappers** (`#el-<sid>`), no injected overlay DOM, no
per-scene cooperation. Overlay families (staggered blocks, blinds, light leak, grid
dissolve, page burn) and shader transitions are deferred to later phases.

## Stage ground prerequisite (white-flash guard)

Several templates open a window where the two wrappers' summed opacity < 1 (the
cut-the-curve mid-window cut, zoom-through's 0.15 floor, plain crossfade's
power-curve dip). Whatever is BEHIND the wrappers shows through during that
window. If the assembled `index.html` `#root` has no opaque background, the
renderer composites the dip over its default **white** page → a white flash at
every seam, glaring on dark films (observed on two Spotify runs before the fix).
**The assembler must paint the stage:** `#root { background:
var(--canvas-deep, var(--canvas, #000)) }` — `assemble-index.mjs` now emits this;
any other consumer of these templates owns the same guarantee.

## How the injector applies a transition

At a `break` boundary between scene _i_ (`from`) and scene _i+1_ (`to`), the
injector:

1. Extends `#el-<from>` wrapper `data-duration` by `duration_s` (holds its final
   frame — verified: `core/src/runtime/init.ts:1393-1410` external-slot branch).
2. Pulls `#el-<to>` wrapper `data-start` earlier by `duration_s` (creates the
   overlap window).
3. Reassigns **all** clip `data-track-index` as a 0/1 ping-pong so the two
   overlapping wrappers never share a track (same-track overlap is illegal —
   `core/src/lint/rules/composition.ts`). Higher track composites on top.
4. Stamps the `gsap_template` into `window.__timelines["main"]` at `T = overlap-start`.

Verified by prototype render (2026-05-31): the master-timeline wrapper tween is
seeked and rendered (no double-seek with the sub-comp's own paused timeline —
the runtime drives them independently), the extended wrapper holds scene _i_'s
final frame, and the higher-track incoming wrapper composites over + blends with
the outgoing one.

## Template placeholders

The injector substitutes these tokens in each `gsap_template` line:

| Token                              | Meaning                                                                  |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `__OLD__`                          | `"#el-<from>"` — outgoing clip wrapper selector (quoted)                 |
| `__NEW__`                          | `"#el-<to>"` — incoming clip wrapper selector (quoted)                   |
| `__T__`                            | overlap-start time in seconds (master clock)                             |
| `__DUR__`                          | `duration_s` for this boundary                                           |
| `__DX__`                           | horizontal travel for directional types: `-1920` (LEFT) / `1920` (RIGHT) |
| `__DY__`                           | vertical travel: `-1080` (UP) / `1080` (DOWN)                            |
| `__ORIGIN_OUT__` / `__ORIGIN_IN__` | transformOrigin pair for `squeeze`                                       |

`filter` / `scaleX` / `transformOrigin` are lint-clean on the master timeline
(verified: `core/src/lint/rules/gsap.ts` has no per-property whitelist and scopes
its checks to `data-composition-id` ranges; the x/y/scale/rotation/opacity
whitelist is a _scene-worker_ prompt rule only — it does not bind index.html).

Budget roughly 350 MB per live instance; run one at a time. - External runtime dependencies: `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/gsap@3.14.2/dist/gsap.min.js`, `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js`, `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/postprocessing/EffectComposer.js`, `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/postprocessing/RenderPass.js`, `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/postprocessing/BokehPass.js`. - Web fonts from Google Fonts: Gelasio. ## Editing rules (from the source project) 1. Keep `data-composition-variables` a single-quoted attribute with plain `"` JSON. Never save it through Studio's Design panel. 2. Do not put `` in static markup; create it at runtime. 3. Keep every visual state a function of t; seek-safety is what makes the block renderable.

skills.text:
--- name: cuboid-carousel description: A chain of bevelled cuboids rides a travelling wave as a content carousel. HyperFrames block, 1920×1080, 6.666666666666667s, 40 variables. --- # Cuboid Carousel Rounded, bevelled cuboids carrying card content fly in from the right as one rigid group, cruise with a per-cuboid rotation stagger, decelerate to a hero hold, then exit left. Spacing is derived from the cuboid dimensions and the largest reachable X half-extent, so cuboids can never overlap. skills.name: figma
skills.description: Bring Figma into a HyperFrames video - rendered assets, brand tokens, components, storyboard frames as reconstructed motion (frames read as states, not slides), shaders and connector-assisted motion. Use when the person pastes a figma.com link or asks to use a Figma design, frame, logo or brand.
skills.category: 视频框架与程序化成片
skills.text:
---
name: figma
description: Bring Figma into a HyperFrames video - rendered assets, brand tokens, components, storyboard frames as reconstructed motion (frames read as states, not slides), shaders and connector-assisted motion. Use when the person pastes a figma.com link or asks to use a Figma design, frame, logo or brand.
---

**Plugin installs:** Before setup or freshness commands, follow [plugin execution rules](../hyperframes/references/plugin-installation.md) when this skill is inside a HyperFrames plugin.

# Figma → HyperFrames

Every import happens at build time and freezes a local file with its source recorded under `.media/`, so renders never call Figma and re-running a command re-imports only what changed. Assets, tokens and components go over REST with a token; motion and shader data need a Figma connector, or a native export from the person.

## Access

`FIGMA_TOKEN` in the shell or the project `.env`. Check it exists before the first command; if not, tell the person how to make one and stop: figma.com → Settings → Security → Personal access tokens, read-only **File content** and **File metadata**, plus **Library content** for `tokens` on non-Enterprise plans. They set it themselves; never ask them to paste it into the chat.

| Error | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `BAD_TOKEN` (401) | Expired or revoked: make a new one |
| `FORBIDDEN` (403) | The message names the missing scope, or the file isn't visible to the account |
| `REQUIRES_ENTERPRISE` (403, variables) | Not a failure: the published-styles fallback already ran |
| `RATE_LIMITED` (429) | Already retried with backoff; wait a minute or import fewer nodes per call |

## Commands

- A layer, logo or image: `npx hyperframes figma asset '<url or fileKey:nodeId>' [more refs] --format svg|png --scale 2 --description "<what it is>" [--entity "<brand mark>"]`. SVG for vectors and logos, PNG at 2x for raster. Several nodes of one file in one call render in a single request; `--entity` lets `/media-use` find a brand mark later.
- Brand colours and type: `npx hyperframes figma tokens <fileKey>`. Run it before `component` and paste the printed entries into `data-composition-variables`. Without Enterprise it falls back to published styles. A connector can supply variables there instead: cache its raw response in `.media/figma-cache/` and write the bindings to `.media/figma-bindings.jsonl` (`{kind:"binding", figmaId, sourceFileKey, compositionVariableId:"figma:<name>", version}`).
- A frame as editable HTML at exact geometry: `npx hyperframes figma component '<url or fileKey:nodeId>'`, packaged under `compositions/components/<name>/`. A fill bound to an imported token comes out as `var(--slug, #literal)`, so one variable re-brands every import; an unknown token stays a literal marked `data-figma-unresolved`: import that library's tokens and re-import. Ask once which file a library is; never match by hex.
- Check hero components against Figma's pixels (`figma asset <same node> --format png`). Text drift is the usual cause; report drift you can't fix instead of hand-tweaking the import.

## Motion (connector)

Usage beacon: these phases have no CLI touchpoint, so run `npx hyperframes events --skill=figma-motion` when you begin and `npx hyperframes events --skill=figma-motion --event=skill_completed --outcome=success|error` when done. Same for shaders (`figma-shaders`) and storyboards (`figma-storyboard`).

1. Fetch motion context for the parent frame in one recursive request; cache the raw JSON in `.media/figma-cache/`.
2. Normalise with `motionContextToDocs(raw, { selectorFor, repeat })` from `@hyperframes/core/figma`, never by transcribing keyframes. It reads the motion.dev snippets (the CSS snippets stretch durations), drops loop-wrap tail keyframes and keeps bezier eases. `selectorFor` returns the ids from the component import.
3. `motionToGsap(doc)` → `emitTimelineScript(spec)`, injected after the GSAP and CustomEase tags: paused, finite, a literal `window.__timelines` key. Named eases outside the mapped set fall back to linear; say so.
4. Verify against Figma's own export: `node <SKILL_DIR>/scripts/verify-motion.mjs --reference <export.mp4> --render <render.mp4> --crop WxH+X+Y`. It compares motion between samples, so static drift cancels out, and fails under 15 dB (faithful ≈ 20+, diverging ≈ 5). Measure `--crop` from the render's card edges. A fail means fix the translation, not the threshold.
5. A track that won't translate: export it, freeze the MP4 and place it as `<video class="clip">`.

## Shaders

Figma's export path flattens shaders to their base colour, and shader source is only reachable for library-published styles. Ask the person for a native export of that frame (PNG or MP4) and place it as an asset or clip.

## Storyboards: frames are KEYFRAMES, not slides

Two frames holding the same element describe that element's state through time: animate the element between the states. Playing the frames back to back as stills is the failure mode.

1. Scenes are every frame-sized node in the section, named frames and loose full-frame rectangles alike: filter by size, not type or name. Order by `absoluteBoundingBox.x`.
2. Match children across neighbouring frames by name first, then by similar size and position. Tween geometry between states; crossfade two exports in place when the pixels changed. Export one asset per element, not one still per frame. Unmatched children enter or exit at their scene's beat.
3. Text nodes below the strip are motion notes for the scene above them, not on-screen copy. A note about motion inside a scene ("lines reveal one after another") means import that frame as a component and animate it.
4. Export in batches of about 4 scene frames per call: past about 12 ids `/v1/images` times out.
5. Frames that are one product UI in successive states: rebuild the UI as live DOM: code what changes state, freeze what doesn't, and treat each frame change as an interaction to perform (the cursor moves, clicks, the screen responds), not a tween to apply.
6. Stills are the fallback, only for frames with no shared elements.

Never leave a Figma URL in the composition.

skills.name: hyperframes-cli
skills.description: The HyperFrames CLI by job - scaffold, check, look at frames, edit the timeline, preview, render locally or in the cloud, publish, project history - plus reading its JSON and recovering from build or render failures.
skills.category: 视频框架与程序化成片
skills.text:
---
name: hyperframes-cli
description: The HyperFrames CLI by job - scaffold, check, look at frames, edit the timeline, preview, render locally or in the cloud, publish, project history - plus reading its JSON and recovering from build or render failures.
---

**Plugin installs:** Before setup or freshness commands, follow [plugin execution rules](../hyperframes/references/plugin-installation.md) when this skill is inside a HyperFrames plugin.

# HyperFrames CLI

Run `npx hyperframes <command>` unless the project gives a wrapper; then use the wrapper. It needs Node.js 22+ and FFmpeg. Every command has `--help`; most take `--json`, and a failure prints `✗ …`, a `Fix:` line and exits non-zero.

## Commands by job

| Job | Commands |
| --- | --- |
| Start | `init <dir>` (blank; `--example <name>` only when asked), `capture <url>` |
| Read a project | `info`, `compositions`, `timeline --json`, `docs <topic>` |
| Check it | `lint` while writing; `check --json` as the gate (lint, runtime, layout, contrast) |
| Look at it | `snapshot` (`--at <t,…>`, `--range START,END`, `--composition <id>`, `--zoom`, `--angle`, `--against <video>`), `keyframes`, `compare`, `audio` |
| Edit the timeline | `timeline` with `move`, `trim`, `split`, `set`, `duplicate`, `delete`, `apply`, `undo`, `ids` |
| Reuse | `catalog`, `add` (`/hyperframes-registry`) |
| Media and sound | `media-treatment`, `grade-compare`, `remove-background`, `tts`, `transcribe`, `beats`, `normalize-audio` (`/media-use`) |
| Show and ship | `preview`, `present` (`/slideshow`), `render`, `publish`, `cloud`, `lambda`, `cloudrun` |
| Desktop app | `open`, `catch-up` |
| Upkeep | `doctor`, `browser`, `upgrade`, `skills`, `usage`, `clean`, `feedback` |

`validate`, `inspect` and `layout` are deprecated aliases of `check`; `events` is telemetry for skills' own scripts. Don't run them.

## The loop

1. Write, then `npx hyperframes lint` after the first pass and after structural changes.
2. `npx hyperframes check --json` and fix every error. While a lint error remains the layout and contrast audits don't run; "0 samples" means nothing was checked. Contrast failures carry a `suggestedColor`. A finding at a single sample (an entrance in flight) is info; a 3 s+ video with no visible change fails `sweep_static`.
3. `npx hyperframes snapshot` and read the PNGs (under `.hyperframes/artifacts/snapshots/`): that is how you see the video. With sub-compositions, snapshot a midpoint of every scene; tiny unstyled content or a missing hero is a mount defect (`../hyperframes/references/format.md`).
4. `npx hyperframes preview --background`, check the URL answers 200, give the person the project URL and wait, unless they asked for the file or for no stops. Passing checks alone is not a reason to render.
5. When it is time to render (step 4): `npx hyperframes render --quality looks --output out.mp4` (`draft` while iterating, `delivery` for the final). Confirm the file is non-empty and its `ffprobe` duration matches the root `data-duration`, then look at decoded frames.

"This element" or the current selection: `npx hyperframes preview --context --json --context-fields selection`; `no-selection` means ask them to click it.

## Edit the timeline

These are the edits Studio itself makes, so the result stays in Studio's shape.

- `timeline --json` lists clips with absolute `absStart`/`absEnd`, owning `file` and the `#id` ref the edit commands take (`timeline ids` stamps missing ids).
- `timeline move|trim|split|set|duplicate|delete <ref> … --plan --json` previews one edit; run it again without `--plan`. `--start`, `--end`, `--duration` set one edge or the length.
- An edit is refused when the clip would overlap a neighbour (`--overwrite`, or move the neighbour first) or end past its composition: raise the root's `data-duration` first. No command changes `data-duration`.
- Several edits at once: a JSON file such as `[{"verb": "move", "ref": "#outro", "time": "9"}]`, then `timeline apply plan.json --json`. Each run prints a `receipt`; save it and `timeline undo receipt.json` reverts it.

<!-- history (trial): remove this block together with the command -->

## Project history

Every write is kept and can be undone. At the start of a turn, `npx hyperframes history begin --who <you> --label "<plan>"`, then `history --since mine --who <you>` to see what the person changed; build on their edits. A check failed or they say it got worse: `history undo --who <you>`, never hand-edit back. End the turn with `history end`.

<!-- /history (trial) -->

## Render where

| Need | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Local | `render --quality looks --output out.mp4` (`draft`, `delivery`) |
| Reproducible container | `render --docker --strict --output out.mp4` |
| Batch from variables | `render --batch rows.json --output "renders/{name}.mp4"` |
| Hosted, no local Chrome or FFmpeg | `cloud render` (`references/cloud.md`) |
| Your own AWS or GCP | `lambda render`, `cloudrun render` (`references/lambda.md`, `references/cloudrun.md`) |

A 30 s film renders in a minute or two: run it in the foreground. Detach only a render longer than your tool's timeout (`HYPERFRAMES_RENDER_DETACHED=1`, its own group, output to a log) and wait with `until grep -qE 'Render (complete|failed)' render.log; do sleep 5; done`, never `pgrep -f`, which matches its own loop and waits until the tool times out.

After a verified render, send one `feedback --rating`, plus a report for anything the person asked for that HyperFrames can't do, unless telemetry is off: `references/feedback.md`.

## When a command fails

| Symptom | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| Chrome missing or won't start | `npx hyperframes browser ensure`; `doctor --json` always exits 0, gate on `.ok` |
| A heavy page isn't ready in time | Raise `--timeout` on `check` or `snapshot` |
| Unusual codec looks blank | Keep `--proxy` on (the default) |
| Render slow on Linux | The summary's second line says `screenshot` + `software gpu`: the slow path |
| `capture` fails or writes `BLOCKED.md` | Take nothing from its partial files; retry into a new `-o` folder |
| Disk tight | `clean --dry-run`, then `clean`; never delete `.hyperframes` (it holds history) |

# HyperFrames registry

Starting from an item is faster and usually better than writing the effect yourself, and an installed item is ordinary source in your project: change it, cut it down, restyle it.

## Find and install

```bash
npx hyperframes catalog --query "<what the beat should do, in English>" --json
npx hyperframes add <name> --json        # prints the written files and the mount snippet
```

- Query in English even when the video is not: the catalog is indexed in English, and another script returns `No searchable words in query`, which is not a gap.
- Search is local and sends nothing. The default `words` tier only finds items that reuse your words; `--on-device` ranks by meaning after a one-time ~33 MB download. Offer that download and let the person decide; never enable it silently. The `--json` envelope names the tier that answered.
- Narrow with `--type block|component` and `--tag <tag>`. `add <tag>` installs every block with that tag; dependencies install first. `add` needs the network even for an item installed before; search works offline from the cached manifest.
- Nothing fits: report it before you hand-build, on either tier. `catalog --query` prints the line pre-filled (`report_gap` in `--json`): `npx hyperframes feedback --search-miss "<query>" --wanted "<the move you needed>" --tier <tier>`. Describe the effect, not an item name you imagined.

Tiers, `dropped` and `unindexed`, stale indexes, offline behaviour: `references/search.md`.

## What's in it

| Blocks: a scene with its own timeline | Examples |
| --- | --- |
| Transitions | `beat-freeze-cut`, `chromatic-radial-split`, `cinematic-zoom` |
| Overlays and lower thirds | `camcorder-hud`, `editorial-flash-overlay`, `lt-clean-bar` |
| Title cards and kinetic type | `canopy-part-title`, `code-slice-hero` |
| Social, chat and UI cards | `ai-chat-reveal`, `chatgpt-exchange` |
| Code, charts, data and maps | `code-diff`, `bar-chart-race`, `data-chart` |
| 3D, shader and backgrounds | `app-showcase`, `aurora`, `blob` |

| Components: a snippet merged into your scene | Examples |
| --- | --- |
| Motion primitives and text effects | `agent-cursor`, `blur-in`, `bottom-up-letters` |
| Caption styles | `caption-clip-wipe`, `caption-editorial-emphasis` |
| Camera moves | `camera-shake`, `camera-scan-gate` |
| Product demo and UI props | `before-after-wipe`, `browser-device-stage` |
| Textures, particles and effects | `ascii-render-pass`, `grain-overlay` |

## Wiring

- **Block**: installs to `compositions/<name>.html`. Mount it with `data-composition-src`, `data-composition-id` matching the block's own id, `data-start` and the `data-duration` you need; the snippet `add` prints is the starting point. `references/wiring-blocks.md`.
- **Component**: installs to `compositions/components/<name>.html`. Copy its markup, `<style>` and script into your scene, and follow its comment block if it hooks into your timeline. `references/wiring-components.md`.
- Take the largest unit that fits, then edit it. Keep an installed item's ids prefixed as they are, so two items can't collide.
- An item keeps its own variables; set them for one mount with `data-variable-values` on its host (`add --vars '{"title":"…"}'` writes that), and point its colour and font variables at your brand's.
- Beat-synced blocks take hit times from `npx hyperframes beats --json`: the beat times minus the mount's `data-start`.
- Install paths come from `hyperframes.json` (`references/install-locations.md`).

## Contributing

Authoring a new block or component for an upstream PR: `references/contributing.md`, starter templates in `references/templates.md`, quality bar in `references/component-quality-bar.md`.

---
name: hyperframes
description: Read first to make, edit, animate or render any video with HyperFrames (HTML rendered to video), including launch films, explainers, music videos, charts, maps, vertical clips, title cards, captions and overlays. Holds the render contract, the work loop and what each kind of video needs.
---

**Plugin installs:** Before setup or freshness commands, follow [plugin execution rules](references/plugin-installation.md) when this skill is inside a HyperFrames plugin.

# HyperFrames

HyperFrames renders HTML to video by seeking a paused timeline frame by frame, so every render is identical; the person edits the same files in the Studio preview. Use it unless another framework or a plain browser recording is asked for. Run the CLI as `npx hyperframes <command>` (`/hyperframes-cli`); at the start of a new video, `npx hyperframes usage --json` reports the person's remaining plan usage (say "unknown" when it is).

`index.html` is the root composition: it declares the video's variables and mounts one scene per sub-composition from `compositions/`. Media and fonts live in `assets/`. A new project: `npx hyperframes init <dir>`. A website as the subject: `npx hyperframes capture <url> --json`.

Build what was asked: no voiceover or captions and no new aspect ratio unless the request or the source calls for them; a film over ~15 s that tells something gets music and sound on its visible actions unless the person asked for silence (`references/sound.md`). A new video is 1920×1080 at 30 fps. A question, a hold or a loose idea gets an answer or a proposal, not an edit. Before hand-writing a named effect, transition, caption style, chart or card, search the registry (`/hyperframes-registry`). Any media (a presenter or avatar, footage, voice, music): `/media-use`, which says when HeyGen is needed and what is free. Show real things from their source (the product's screens, the brand's logo, a real place's imagery); draw only what has none.

## Contract

`npx hyperframes check --json` reports most violations with a `Fix:` line.

1. Every timed element has `class="clip"`, `data-start` and `data-duration` in seconds, and shows over `[start, start + duration)`: land an end state just before its end. `data-track-index` is only a Studio lane; paint order is `z-index`.
2. The video's length is the root's `data-duration`: overrun is cut, an early end holds the last frame.
3. Each composition builds one paused timeline and registers it after its tweens: `window.__timelines["<data-composition-id>"] = tl`.
4. No `Date.now()`, unseeded `Math.random()`, network fetches, timers or `repeat: -1`. Everything visible is a function of timeline time.
5. Never tween `display`, `visibility` or `autoAlpha` on a `.clip`; animate a child.
6. No CSS `transform` on an element GSAP transforms; animate transforms, not `left`/`top`/`width`/`height`.
7. Never `play()`, `pause()` or seek media. A `<video>` keeps its sound with `data-has-audio="true"`, else it is `muted`; music, voice, replacement sound and J/L cuts are a separate `<audio>`.
8. Every `<audio>` has an `id` or it is left out of the mix. No `crossorigin` on media. Time a `<video>` or its wrapper, never both.
9. Only the bundled fonts (`references/format.md`) resolve by name; any other family needs `@font-face` to a file in `assets/fonts/`.
10. Asset paths are root-relative (`assets/...`), in sub-compositions too.
11. Grades, grain, blur and vignettes on footage go through `npx hyperframes media-treatment` (`/media-use`), never CSS filters.
12. A scene file puts its styles, markup and scripts inside `<template>` and styles its root as `#root`. Intended overflow or overlap: `data-layout-allow-overflow`, `data-layout-allow-overlap`.

## Keep it editable

Studio edits the tags you write.

- One scene per sub-composition, short readable ids; the root holds only scene hosts, media and audio.
- Timed elements are written in the HTML, not made by script, each with a stable `id`.
- Copy, brand colours and swappable media are variables (`data-var-text`, `data-var-src`, `var(--id)`).
- One kind per track: `data-track-kind="graphics"` on scene and overlay hosts, `captions` on the one host that holds every caption group.
- Content stays inside the 90% action-safe box, captions and key text inside 80% title-safe; Studio draws the guides, never add them.

## Work loop

- An existing project: `npx hyperframes timeline --json` shows what plays when; before any change, `npx hyperframes history --since mine --who <you>` shows what the person changed since your last turn: build on it (`/hyperframes-cli`).
- A new film over ~15 s that tells something: its type's file (below), then `references/story.md`: three storylines that are three different films, in words only; the person picks unless they asked for the file or no stops. Then `SPEC.md` (`references/spec.md`): every adjective as a number, the defaults banned by name, the shots by frame.
- After your last edit: `npx hyperframes check --json`; fix every error, weigh every warning. A film: `npx hyperframes snapshot --review` and `references/review.md`, ending in `REVIEW.md`. A small edit: snapshot what you changed (`--at`, `--range`, `--composition`) and look before you reply.
- Render when the person approves the Studio preview, asks for the file or asks for no stops, after your check and review pass; otherwise stop at the preview and wait.

## The HyperFrames desktop app

Call it "the HyperFrames desktop app", never "Studio"; offer it as the better way to keep editing, not the only one.

- Before the delivery render of a new video, open the Studio preview, even in no-questions mode, and say they can edit there. If `preview` printed "Keep editing by chatting with Framey", add that the **Edit with Framey** button opens the app.
- After the delivery render, pass on its Framey line in your own words: offer to run the `hyperframes open` it names or give its download link; else say nothing (autonomous: the delivery note).
- When any command says to run `catch-up`, run `npx hyperframes catch-up [dir]` before your next change; what it lists is their work, not a new request.

## What to read

| The request | Read |
| --- | --- |
| Launch, promo, feature | `references/types/launch.md` |
| Explainer, tutorial | `references/types/explainer.md` |
| Music video | `references/types/music.md` |
| Chart, numbers | `references/types/data.md` |
| Vertical or social clip | `references/types/vertical.md` |
| 3D, simulation, generative | `references/types/3d.md` |
| Character, mascot, story short | `references/types/character.md` |
| A real place or map; a website, PR or script; kinetic type | `references/film.md` |
| Captions; cards over a talking head | `references/captions.md`; `references/overlays.md` |
| Motion: eases, titles, cuts, punch-ins, speed, holds | `references/motion.md` |
| Scenes, attributes, media, lint; GSAP, Lottie, 3D, canvas | `references/format.md`; `references/runtimes.md` |

Decks: `/slideshow`. Remotion source: `/remotion-to-hyperframes`. Figma: `/figma`. Installing, refreshing or upgrading skills and the pinned CLI: `references/skill-lifecycle.md`.

description: Bring existing video code or footage into HyperFrames and verify it frame by frame against the original - Remotion first, also Motion Canvas, Lottie, Three.js, p5.js, canvas or plain HTML/CSS animation, or renders from Manim, After Effects or Blender. Use to port, convert, migrate or reuse work made with another tool.

**Plugin installs:** Before setup or freshness commands, follow [plugin execution rules](../hyperframes/references/plugin-installation.md) when this skill is inside a HyperFrames plugin.

# Import into HyperFrames

HyperFrames is the container: its tracks, sub-compositions and variables are editable in Studio whatever runs inside a clip. Bring each part in at the highest level it supports and record which level you used.

| Level | For | How | Editable in Studio afterwards |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Native | code that can become HTML + GSAP: most Remotion, HTML/CSS/GSAP animation, simple Motion Canvas | translate it, then verify frame by frame | every element; variables, catalog, presets apply |
| Hosted | code that can draw any requested frame in a browser: canvas, p5.js, Three.js, Lottie, WebGL, other JS animation | keep the code and drive it from HyperFrames time | timing, position, exposed parameters |
| Media | anything that outputs video or frames: Manim, After Effects, Blender, PIL, moviepy | render to a file and use it as a clip | cut, place, layer; not the pixels inside |

Code that depends on wall-clock time, live physics or the network can only come in as media.

## Native: translate, then verify

1. For Remotion, run `python3 <SKILL_DIR>/scripts/lint_source.py <source dir>` first. Blockers (`useState`, `useReducer`, `useEffect` with dependencies, async `calculateMetadata`, React UI kits such as MUI, Chakra, Mantine, antd, shadcn, Radix, NextUI) don't translate: host them or refactor them out, never approximate (`references/escape-hatch.md`). Warnings (`@remotion/lambda` config, `delayRender`, `useMemo`, custom hooks) are dropped and noted.
2. Translate to the `/hyperframes` contract: one sub-composition per scene, times in seconds (`frame / fps`), asset paths root-relative. Each Remotion API's equivalent is in `references/api-map.md`.
3. Keep it editable: the source's props become `data-composition-variables` bound with `data-var-text`, `data-var-src` or `var(--id)`; each `Sequence` becomes a timed clip or a sub-composition; a reused component becomes one sub-composition mounted several times with `data-variable-values`.
4. Compare frame by frame: `npx hyperframes snapshot --at <t,…> --against <original.mp4>` saves the original's frame at each time next to yours. Sample every scene and both sides of every cut; look for one late or recoloured element, not only the overall picture. For a scored check, `scripts/render_diff.sh <original.mp4> <hf.mp4> <out>` gives SSIM per frame and `scripts/frame_strip.sh` shows which frames diverged (thresholds per complexity tier in `references/eval.md`). Render the Remotion side with `Config.setVideoImageFormat("png")` and `Config.setColorSpace("bt709")`, or the diff measures the encoders (about 0.05 SSIM).
5. Write what didn't translate cleanly (dropped volume ramps, approximated presentations, substituted fonts) to `TRANSLATION_NOTES.md`.

| Remotion | Read |
| --- | --- |
| `Composition`, `defaultProps`, `schema`, `calculateMetadata` | `references/parameters.md` |
| `Sequence`, `Series`, `Loop`, `AbsoluteFill`, `Freeze` | `references/sequencing.md` |
| `useCurrentFrame`, `interpolate`, `spring`, `Easing`, `interpolateColors` | `references/timing.md` |
| `Audio`, `Video`, `Img`, `IFrame`, `staticFile`, `delayRender` | `references/media.md` |
| `TransitionSeries`, `@remotion/transitions` | `references/transitions.md` |
| `@remotion/lottie` | `references/lottie.md` |
| `@remotion/google-fonts`, `Font.loadFont`, `@font-face` | `references/fonts.md` |
| What can't be ported | `references/limitations.md` |

Before hand-building a named visual the source used, search `npx hyperframes catalog --query "<the visual, in English>" --json`: it ranks the whole registry with nothing installed.

## Hosted

Keep the code and let HyperFrames own the clock: it draws the frame for the time it is given. The seek protocol and the built-in adapters for Lottie, Three.js, anime.js, WAAPI and CSS animations are in `../hyperframes/references/runtimes.md`. No `requestAnimationFrame` loop or timer as the time source, seeded randomness only, and `data-duration` on the root when nothing else defines the length.

## Media

`<video class="clip" data-has-audio="true" src="assets/x.mp4" ...>`, or `muted` when it is silent. Nothing else is needed.

In the final message, list each imported part with its level, what a person can change in Studio, and how the frame-by-frame comparison came out.

---
name: slideshow
description: Build a HyperFrames slideshow to present live - slides, fragment reveals, branching hotspots and presenter mode with speaker notes, served by `hyperframes present` - or turn an existing page into one. Use when the person wants a deck or presentation rather than a rendered video.
---

**Plugin installs:** Before setup or freshness commands, follow [plugin execution rules](../hyperframes/references/plugin-installation.md) when this skill is inside a HyperFrames plugin.

# HyperFrames slideshow

A slideshow is a normal composition (the `/hyperframes` contract applies) plus one JSON island that says which scenes are slides and how they connect. The deliverable is a running deck, not an MP4.

## What changes from a video project

- **Each slide is a top-level scene** in the composition file: `data-composition-id`, `data-start`, `data-duration`, `data-label`, `data-width`, `data-height`. There is no master root composition wrapping them.
- **One island per composition**, near the top of `<body>`, written in the HTML (never generated by script; `present` reads the file statically):

```html
<script type="application/hyperframes-slideshow+json">
  {
    "slides": [
      { "sceneId": "hook", "notes": "Pause on the number." },
      {
        "sceneId": "problem",
        "fragments": [11.0, 15.0],
        "hotspots": [
          {
            "id": "h1",
            "label": "Where does $40B come from?",
            "target": "market-detail",
            "region": { "x": 55, "y": 60, "w": 40, "h": 20 }
          }
        ]
      }
    ],
    "slideSequences": [
      { "id": "market-detail", "label": "Market sizing", "slides": [{ "sceneId": "mkt-math" }] }
    ]
  }
</script>
```

- `sceneId` equals a scene's `data-composition-id` (or give `startTime`/`endTime`). `notes` are presenter-only. `ttsScript`, `ttsAudioUrl` and `ttsDurationMs` are reserved and not wired yet.
- **Fragments are absolute timeline times** (the same clock as `data-start`, not offsets inside the slide) within the slide's `[start, end]`. Navigation seeks, it never plays: each hold state must look right when the timeline is seeked straight to that time. A slide without fragments enters at a rest frame inside it.
- **Branch slides** are ordinary scenes listed only in `slideSequences`, never in the main `slides` array. A hotspot's `target` is a sequence `id`; `region` is a percentage box (omit it for a full-slide button). Back returns to the slide that held the hotspot.
- Text the audience must read is at least 40 px at 1920×1080. Before hand-building any named visual, search `npx hyperframes catalog --query "<the visual, in English>" --json`: it ranks the whole registry with nothing installed.

## Porting an existing page

- Keep the source's look, motion, interactions and media behaviour; port its widgets, players and visualizers rather than approximating them.
- Movement the page drove by scroll, wheel or a camera layer becomes a camera move from one focal point to the next on slide navigation, never a page visibly scrolling. Keep each move direct, without reversals the source doesn't make.
- Screenshots, posts, charts, code and any image with readable text are evidence: keep their aspect (`object-fit: contain`) and check all four edges for crops.
- Every copied `<video>`/`<audio>` needs `data-start` and `data-duration` (`data-has-audio="true"` when its sound plays), and no `preload="none"`. Custom media chrome reads the native element's events and `currentTime`, never its own timer.
- Hidden stacked slides need `opacity: 0`, `visibility: hidden` and `pointer-events: none` together, or an invisible layer swallows clicks.

## Present and hand off

- **Never render a deck to MP4**: `render` keeps only the first scene and truncates silently. For stills, `snapshot --at` each slide.
- Run `npx hyperframes check --json` until it is clean. The slideshow rule checks that every `sceneId` resolves, every hotspot `target` exists, fragments sit inside their slide, and main-line slides don't overlap.
- Serve it with `npx hyperframes present <project-dir>` and hand over the URL it prints: "Click Present, or press P, to open the audience tab."
- The project's root `index.html` should open as a working deck: `<hyperframes-slideshow>` around `<hyperframes-player src="…">`, with the raw composition in a subfolder if needed. The component owns Present (P), Prev/Next, the counter, global mute, fullscreen, swipe, hotspots, presenter notes (editable, kept per deck) and stopping media on slide exit. Don't build your own versions of any of these.
- Screen sharing: in Google Meet share the audience **tab**, which keeps rendering in the background. In Zoom drag the audience tab into its own window and share that; a fully covered window freezes.
- A deck opened from the bare player bundle without `present` needs workarounds: `references/standalone-harness.md`.

name: higgsfield-brandkit
description: |

NOT for unbranded image generation (use higgsfield-generate), product catalog photography (use higgsfield-product-photoshoot), website implementation (use higgsfield-websites), or native Figma/Canva/PSD/AI delivery.
argument-hint: "[brand brief or existing assets] [requested deliverables]"

# Higgsfield Brandkit

Build a coherent identity and its requested applications. Treat supplied brand facts and official assets as fixed constraints.

## Bootstrap

1. Resolve `SKILL_ROOT` to this skill's installed directory and create a durable project directory:

   ```bash
   BRANDKIT_WORKDIR="${PWD}/brandkit"
   BRANDKIT_STATE="${BRANDKIT_WORKDIR}/state.json"
   mkdir -p "${BRANDKIT_WORKDIR}"
   ```

2. Read [prerequisites](references/prerequisites.md). Check tools before the stage that needs them. Never install system packages without the user's permission.
3. If `higgsfield` is missing, install it only after permission:

   ```bash
   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/higgsfield-ai/cli/main/install.sh | sh
   ```

4. If `higgsfield account status` fails with an authentication or workspace error, ask the user to run `higgsfield auth login` or select a workspace, then wait.
5. Inspect live model contracts before paid generation:

   ```bash
   higgsfield model get recraft_v4_1 --json
   higgsfield model get seedream_v5_pro --json
   higgsfield model get gpt_image_2 --json
   ```

## CLI mapping

| Operation | Command |
|---|---|
| Discover a model | `higgsfield model get <model> --json` |
| Generate and poll | `higgsfield generate create <model> ... --wait --json` |
| Resume a job | `higgsfield generate wait <job_id> --json` |
| Upload a local asset | `higgsfield upload create <path> --json` |
| Import website metadata | `higgsfield marketing-studio brand-kits fetch --url <url> --wait --json` |
| Read/write approval state | `python3 "$SKILL_ROOT/scripts/brandkit.py" state ...` |
| Render review boards | `python3 "$SKILL_ROOT/scripts/brandkit.py" preview ...` |
| Inspect selected logo | `python3 "$SKILL_ROOT/scripts/brandkit.py" logo-inspect ...` |
| Export logo files | `python3 "$SKILL_ROOT/scripts/brandkit.py" logo-export ...` |
| Build a Brandbook | `python3 "$SKILL_ROOT/scripts/brandkit.py" brandbook-build ...` |

Local image paths passed with `--image` are auto-uploaded. Keep HTML, SVG, PPTX, and PDF deliverables as local project files unless the user explicitly needs a hosted copy.

## User-facing behavior

- Match the user's language. Keep Design Brain reasoning, prompts, state mechanics, scripts, model lookup, and QA internals private.
- Send at most one short status sentence per visible generation batch, then stay quiet until the result is ready.
- Ask one compact set of only unresolved blocking questions. Never repeat facts or force a complete identity questionnaire for a partial task.
- After each palette, logo, typography, or downstream review, stop and wait for ordinary user feedback.
- Never infer approval from silence, successful generation, or your own preference.
- Preserve exact user copy. Never invent positioning, values, claims, ingredients, prices, certifications, statistics, or regulatory content.

## Core workflow

1. **Classify the request.**
   - `apply-existing`: use supplied official assets without redesigning them.
   - `extend-partial`: create only missing slots required by the requested output.
   - `create-identity`: create a new logo or identity only when explicitly requested.
2. **Read state.** Run:

   ```bash
   python3 "$SKILL_ROOT/scripts/brandkit.py" state \
     --state-file "$BRANDKIT_STATE" --action get_status
   ```

   Local state is durable. Never paste, hand-edit, or recreate approvals when the state file exists.
3. **Run intake and asset analysis.** Read [intake](references/intake.md), [asset analysis](references/asset-analysis.md), [state routing](references/handoff.md), and [exact state payloads](references/state-payloads.md). Lock every user-declared official logo, palette, and typography slot immediately.
4. **Create the Brand Lock.** Read [Brand Lock](references/brand-lock.md). Record exact spelling, official assets, colors, fonts, layout/shape rules, requested outputs, and forbidden treatments.
5. **Require only the slots the output uses.**
   - logo-only → palette + logo for a new mark; official logo alone for an existing mark
   - palette-only → palette
   - typography-only → typography
   - copy-free mockup/merch → logo; add palette only when color/application requires it
   - text-bearing social/packaging/poster/signage → logo + palette + typography
   - Brandbook/deck → logo + palette + typography
6. **Build missing foundation slots.** Read [Design Brain](references/brandkit-design-brain.md), [concept boards](references/concept-boards.md), [inline reviews](references/inline-widgets.md), and only the needed [palette](references/palette.md), [logo](references/logo.md), or [typography](references/typography.md) module.
7. **Continue the original request** as soon as its required slots are approved. Never ask the user to choose scope again.
8. **Load only the requested production module:**
   - [mockups](references/mockups.md)
   - [social graphics](references/social-templates.md)
   - [posters/banners](references/posters-banners.md)
   - [packaging](references/packaging.md)
   - [signage](references/signage.md)
   - [merchandise](references/merchandise.md)
   - [presentation decks](references/presentation-deck.md)
   - [Brandbooks](references/brandbook.md)
9. **QA and approval.** Read [QA and iteration](references/qa-and-iteration.md). Repair only the failing output. Save a downstream element only after explicit approval with its exact foundation dependencies.

## New identity sequence

### 1. Palette

Render 2–3 exact palette options as deterministic HTML using [preview payloads](references/preview-payloads.md). Show PNG screenshots plus editable HTML files and wait. Persist the selected palette with `approve_palette` before logo generation.

### 2. SVG logo marks

Read [logo prompt enhancer](references/logo-prompt-enhancer.md). Produce exactly three distinct symbol-only mechanisms and one Recraft prompt for each. Write each long prompt to a file and submit separately:

```bash
higgsfield generate create recraft_v4_1 \
  --model_type vector \
  --colors @"${BRANDKIT_WORKDIR}/logo-colors.json" \
  --background_color '#F7F7F5' \
  --aspect_ratio 1:1 \
  --resolution 2k \
  --wait --json < "${BRANDKIT_WORKDIR}/logo-candidate-1.txt"
```

Use the returned SVG URLs directly for review. After selection, inspect the exact SVG without altering it:

```bash
python3 "$SKILL_ROOT/scripts/brandkit.py" logo-inspect \
  --source "<selected Recraft SVG URL or absolute local path>"
```

Persist the exact job ID, SVG URL, name, palette revision, and returned canonical geometry fingerprint with `approve_logo`.

### 3. Typography

Propose 2–3 unique display/body pairs using supplied fonts or verified Google Fonts. Render the real brand name and sample copy through the preview script. Persist only the selected pair with `approve_typography`.

Interactive flows always stop for palette, logo, and typography selections. Explicit no-question mode may choose and persist a palette, but it still shows all three SVG logo candidates and stops for the user's logo selection; exact brand marks are never self-approved.

## Consistency invariants

- Reuse the same approved logo source everywhere. Never redraw an official or selected SVG when deterministic placement/export is possible.
- A generated logo depends on the palette revision used to create it. Changing that palette invalidates the generated logo and its dependents; changing typography does not invalidate the symbol mark.
- Changing a foundation slot invalidates only downstream elements that list that slot in `required_slots`.
- Copy the same Brand Lock values into every related generation prompt: exact hex, font roles, shape language, placement, clear space, composition, and forbidden treatments.
- Use Recraft V4.1 vector mode only for new logo marks.
- Use Seedream as the primary photoreal mockup generator. Use GPT Image 2 only for the controlled stage that adds readable text or exact graphic details.
- Use local deterministic SVG/PPTX/HTML construction for exact copy and editable layouts. Do not ask an image model to fake editable files.
- Do not promise native Figma, Canva, PSD, AI, or EPS files.

## Deterministic scripts

Create JSON input files under `"$BRANDKIT_WORKDIR"`; never interpolate user text directly into shell arguments.

```bash
python3 "$SKILL_ROOT/scripts/brandkit.py" preview \
  --input "$BRANDKIT_WORKDIR/reviews.json" \
  --output-dir "$BRANDKIT_WORKDIR/reviews"

python3 "$SKILL_ROOT/scripts/brandkit.py" logo-export \
  --input "$BRANDKIT_WORKDIR/logo-export.json" \
  --output-dir "$BRANDKIT_WORKDIR/logo"

python3 "$SKILL_ROOT/scripts/brandkit.py" brandbook-build \
  --state-file "$BRANDKIT_STATE" \
  --input "$BRANDKIT_WORKDIR/brandbook.json" \
  --output-dir "$BRANDKIT_WORKDIR/brandbook"
```

For logo export, load [logo export payloads](references/logo-export-payloads.md). For Brandbooks, use the bundled builder only; never substitute an improvised PowerPoint or PDF generator after a deterministic contract failure.

## Failure policy

- Retry a failed Recraft or image-generation request once with the same locked concept and corrected contract. Stop after the second equivalent failure.
- If preview or logo export fails twice, report the concrete error; never replace it with ad-hoc SVG rewriting.
- If the Brandbook template, font, or conversion contract fails, stop immediately. Do not produce a visually different fallback and call it canonical.
- If exact typography or official-logo fidelity cannot be preserved, disclose the limitation instead of claiming completion.
- Never expose raw auth tokens or credentials in files, logs, or chat.

## Delivery

For Brandbooks, follow the strict response contract in [brandbook](references/brandbook.md): PPTX link/path, PDF link/path, and font-install warning only.

For other outputs return:

1. The requested visual files and previews.
2. A compact Brand Lock summary.
3. Editable versus flattened format labels.
4. Required-font/import limitations.
5. Stable variant names for targeted revisions.

## Reference index

- [Prerequisites](references/prerequisites.md) — stage-specific local dependencies and install commands.
- [Intake](references/intake.md) — minimal questions and input routing.
- [Asset analysis](references/asset-analysis.md) — official/reference classification and measurement.
- [State routing](references/handoff.md) and [state payloads](references/state-payloads.md) — persistent approvals.
- [Brand Lock](references/brand-lock.md) — canonical visual constraints.
- [Design Brain](references/brandkit-design-brain.md) — private art direction.
- [Concept boards](references/concept-boards.md), [preview payloads](references/preview-payloads.md), and [inline reviews](references/inline-widgets.md) — selection stages.
- [Logo](references/logo.md), [logo prompt enhancer](references/logo-prompt-enhancer.md), and [logo export payloads](references/logo-export-payloads.md) — SVG generation and deterministic variants.
- [Palette](references/palette.md) and [typography](references/typography.md) — foundation slots.
- [Mockups](references/mockups.md), [social graphics](references/social-templates.md), [posters/banners](references/posters-banners.md), [packaging](references/packaging.md), [signage](references/signage.md), and [merchandise](references/merchandise.md) — applications.
- [Presentation decks](references/presentation-deck.md) and [Brandbooks](references/brandbook.md) — editable documents.
- [QA and iteration](references/qa-and-iteration.md) — preflight, repair, approval, and delivery manifest.
