skills.text:
---
name: scenario-blender-animation
description: "Use when animating characters or objects in Blender through Python, a bouncing ball, walk or run cycle, jump, acting shot, lip sync, eye darts or facial animation, blocking in stepped keys, splining, polish, timing and spacing, arcs, overlap, squash and stretch, graph editor handles, slotted actions or NLA layers, staging a playblast, or when animation looks floaty, stiff, slides, pops, chatters, the subject is too small in frame, or a knee pops and needs an expert review."
license: MIT
---

# Blender animation (character and object)

Expert animation means every frame on screen is a choice: key poses the audience reads, holds and
snaps placed by hand, spacing designed, arcs checked. The Blender Studio stance is to block stepped,
spline late and in parts, and judge from the shot camera at real speed. An agent cannot scrub, so it
measures instead: per-frame positions, spacing charts, arc checks, framing, an onion-skin image, a
curve plot, and a playblast it actually looks at. If a sibling skill named here is missing from your
available skills, ask the user to install it (`npx skills add scenario-labs/skills --skill <name>`);
unattended, proceed from tool schemas and flag the gap.

**REQUIRED BACKGROUND:** scenario-blender-expert (execution channel, review loop, 5.2 API changes).
Shot planning, cameras and animatics belong to scenario-blender-previs-storyboard; building the rig
to scenario-blender-rigging. A clip that guides a render-to-real video model belongs to
scenario-blender-blockout: the model copies keyed limbs as they are, so its cast styles often hand
it a limbless stand-in and let it animate the gait.

Toolkit: [`scripts/bx_anim.py`](scripts/bx_anim.py) (keying, blocking-to-spline, curve checks,
measurement, staging, playblast light, knee-pop, flip and balance checks, onion-skin and curve
images, one-object `bouncing_ball`; API in procedures.md, tested on 5.2.1) and
`bx_review.playblast`.

## Stance (the expert delta)

- **Stay stepped long ("Blocking+").** Hjalti Hjalmarsson: juniors spline too early; computer
  in-betweens are "unintentional interpolated poses" that make notes hard. Keep adding hand-made
  breakdowns while stepped; splining is short and late.
- **Never convert the whole blocking to Bezier.** Rik Schutte: key every main control on every key
  pose, copy each pose to the end of its hold ("pillars"), then spline the body only; face and
  fingers stay stepped until their own pass. Measured on 5.2.1: the naive conversion drifted 84% of
  the next move across a hold, the pillars held at exactly 0.
- **Snaps are authored.** Rik: hold, then change pose in 2 to 3 frames; only big deliberate moves
  are left to interpolation. [added, measured] A contact inside continuous motion (a jump landing)
  is not a hold: pillaring it cut the body's speed at impact from 0.101 to 0.007 m per frame, a
  floaty landing.
- **Odd frames, even gaps; breakdowns shape arcs and steer the eye.** Alex Nagy: key poses on odd
  frames with even spacing so a true middle frame exists. The breakdown sets the arc first, the
  timing second; favoring it late leaves more travel for the last frames, and the fastest part draws
  the eye.
- **The handle type is a timing decision.** AUTO_CLAMPED keeps holds flat; AUTO overshoots between
  two equal keys (Alex uses it to push a pose or cushion a settle); VECTOR for hard hits, contacts
  and take-offs (Alex, Dillon Gu); FREE for burst spacing and exact arcs (Raymond Luc, Joey
  Carlino).
- **Lead with one part, layer the rest.** Rik blocks a torso-only rhythm pass first; Dillon leads
  body mechanics with the COG and acting with the head or eyes. Overlap goes into the blocking, and
  a head never turns on one axis only (Rik).
- **Lip sync is rhythm before shapes.** Rik: jaw first, stepped, opened big only on accents;
  off-sync is a missing preparation, not a global offset; M, B, P closed at least 2 frames and
  closed before the sound.
- **Spacing is felt, arcs are checked, the shot must read.** Raymond: the audience should feel
  spacing tricks, not see them. Pablo Fournier: arcs are the most important check (root, hands,
  feet, nose), in camera space. Hjalti (in scenario-blender-previs-storyboard): after each cut the
  eye must find one thing, so a subject lost in an empty frame fails however good the curves are.

## Establish first

| Input             | Why it changes the plan                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Default when silent                                                      |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Medium, fps       | Film 24 (Hjalti); games often 30 with fixed hit or release frames (Picaut)                                                                                                                                                                                                             | 24 fps                                                                   |
| Camera            | Locked acting shot: judge only through the camera (Rik). Moving, re-framable or gameplay camera: poses work from every direction (Leo Silly-Pelissier, Picaut)                                                                                                                         | locked camera                                                            |
| Style             | Stepped on twos and never splined (Sprite Fright shots, Rik) vs splined; stylized vs naturalistic (Leo)                                                                                                                                                                                | splined, stylized                                                        |
| Rig               | Control names, IK/FK, rotation modes. Generated Rigify [verified]: `torso`, `hips`, `chest`, `head`, `foot_ik.L`, `upper_arm_fk.L`, `jaw_master`; `["IK_FK"]` on `upper_arm_parent.L` (0 IK, 1 FK); legs have `IK_Stretch` 1.0; rest legs are 99.6% straight; main controls QUATERNION | FK arms when arcs matter, IK when hands touch things (Joey, Tony Garcia) |
| Named object      | A brief that names the animated object expects every channel on it                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | one object, `bouncing_ball(obj=...)`                                     |
| Audio, transcript | Beats, accents, phoneme preparation                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | beats from the brief                                                     |
| Reference         | Timing and beats, never a trace (Hjalti)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | none: write a beat list                                                  |
| Budget            | Rik: about 3 s a week in big studios, 5 to 6 s on his acting shot; Flow: 2 s per animator per day                                                                                                                                                                                      | state what the budget buys                                               |

## Workflow

1. **Plan.** Beat list with frames: every acting beat in order (Hjalti counts about 8 per shot),
   sub-beats notice, react, realize, respond (Rik), the leading part per beat. With audio,
   `audio_envelope` + `accent_frames`; hit a pose just before its audio peak (Alex). Start
   mid-action (Rik). GATE: beat table written.
2. **Set up and stage the shot** (P1, P18): fps, range, sound, passepartout 0.99, Simplify for
   previews. Place the camera, then `staging_report(subject, frames)` with the real render size:
   subject height, how much of the frame the action covers, entry, final pose margin. Playblast
   look: `playblast_lighting(key_dir=(0, 0, 1))` (overhead key converted to Workbench's camera
   space: the shadow sits under the subject, the gap is its height, contact is where they meet),
   `floor_slab`, `rotation_texture` on anything that rolls. GATE: `flags` empty; `shadow_frames`
   visible in the air and touching at a contact; camera stills looked at.
3. **Block A, key poses stepped.** Strongest, longest-held pose first (Alex). Build each pose COG,
   feet (weight over the support foot, feet never twins, knees soft), hips, chest, head, arms. Pose
   in world terms with `world_pose` (rig axes are arbitrary), key with
   `key_pose(..., keytype='EXTREME')`, CONSTANT, all main controls. GATE: pose strip
   `onion_skin(frames=keys, spread=...)` shows clear silhouettes and contrast; `balance_report`
   margin >= 0 on held poses.
4. **Blocking+ (still stepped).** `breakdown` at the middle frame with per-part `factors` (COG dips,
   extremities delayed at 0.2 to 0.3, directed part favored late; after a take-off the body is
   ballistic, about 2/3 of the rise in 3 of 7 frames, and the feet must follow); `ease_inbetweens`
   for 20/80 (Pablo); overshoots and settles; overlap offsets; key types as a confidence map
   (Hjalti). GATE: stepped playblast approved; notes on intent stopped (Leo: none after Block B).
5. **Spline the body** with `blocking_to_spline(rig, body_bones, transition=3, interpolate={...})`:
   big moves and continuous contacts in `interpolate`; VECTOR on foot contacts and take-offs. GATE:
   `hold_drift` < 1e-5, `overshoots` only wanted settles, face still CONSTANT, `motion_report`
   without unintended constant spacing, `ballistic_fit` on the airborne COG with `g_ratio` near 1.0
   and a small residual, `limb_extension` never above 1.0.
6. **Re-inject energy** (Leo: splining softens): timing accents, overshoots, desynchronized parts,
   `offset_keys` 1 to 2 frames per chain link (Dillon), head lag 2 to 3 frames in cycles (Joey),
   contacts that slide rather than glue (Rik). Fingers: little overlap, no bounce. GATE: arcs clean
   in camera pixels (`to_camera(..., res=(w, h))`, `motion_report(dims=2)`).
7. **Face and lip sync, stepped** (P6, P7): jaw rhythm, corners (never dead center), shapes from a
   pose library on the lower face minus the jaw, accents and asymmetry in small doses, tongue last,
   then spline the face. Eyes dart in 1 to 2 frames and lead the head; brows 3 to 10 frames (Rik).
   Keys an engine or capture app reads by name (ARKit, visemes): scenario-blender-rigging's
   `shape_report` before keying. GATE: `transitions` meets those counts; accents clearly fewer than
   syllables.
8. **Polish.** `foot_slip` under 1 mm, `lowest_point` for penetration, `rotation_flips` empty
   (`fix_rotation_flips`), `limb_extension` under 0.99 wherever the leg should stay bent, smears 1
   frame (Pablo), burst spacing only now (Raymond), subdivision on. GATE: critique.md rubric passes
   on the final playblast, onion skin and graph image.

**Variants.** Bouncing ball (P16, P18):
`bouncing_ball(obj=ANIM_ball, first_apex=-3, fit=False, ...)` keys ONE object: exact parabolas under
one gravity through whole-frame contacts, odd or even flights so small hops keep their height,
squash on the contact frame and stretch along the velocity through a world-aligned squash modifier
(the roll is never twisted), roll = distance / radius, constant-deceleration roll, a 6-frame hold.
`first_apex` before `start` throws it in from off-screen. Weight mapping is [added]: tune by render.
Walk (Joey, 30 fps): contact 0, down 5, passing 10, up 15, 40-frame cycle; heel curve straight
during contact, root linear with REPEAT_OFFSET (P5). Jump:
`tests/code/blender-animation/test_rigify_jump.py` is the worked example (Rigify human, blocking to
spline).

## Numbers

| Item                              | Value                                                                                                 | Source                             |
| --------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| Snappy pose change                | 2 to 3 frames after the hold                                                                          | Rik                                |
| Aggressive change                 | 4 frames instead of 8                                                                                 | Alex                               |
| Hold to read an idea              | 6 frames                                                                                              | Alex                               |
| Settle                            | 1 to 2 frames, 4 soft                                                                                 | Alex                               |
| Reaction after stimulus           | about 6 frames                                                                                        | Rik                                |
| Eye dart / brow change            | 1 to 2 / 3 to 10 frames                                                                               | Rik                                |
| Ease rule                         | 80% of the remaining way per in-between (slow-in); mirror 20%                                         | Pablo                              |
| Smear                             | 1 frame, sometimes 2                                                                                  | Pablo                              |
| Micro-anticipation                | last 1 to 2 frames before hit or release pushed to an extreme                                         | Picaut                             |
| Head lag in a cycle / foot offset | 2 to 3 frames / 1 frame                                                                               | Joey / Rik                         |
| Real gravity at 24 fps            | acceleration 0.01703 m/frame^2; a quadratic fit's leading coefficient is half (-0.00852). `gravity()` | physics [added]                    |
| Subject size in frame             | 12% of frame height minimum, 15% or more for a single subject                                         | [added] E3: both runs measured 10% |
| IK leg extension                  | under 0.99 of full length while meant bent; above 1.0 = IK stretch                                    | [added]                            |
| Pinwheel on a rolling object      | roll per frame under 360 / sectors degrees                                                            | [added] wagon-wheel                |

## Quality gates

**Measurable:** slot named after the character; key poses CONSTANT and typed before approval;
`hold_drift` ~0; `overshoots` only on settles; `foot_slip` < 1 mm; `lowest_point` never below the
floor (sample sub-frames); `transitions` for darts, brows, snaps, plosives; `ballistic_fit` g_ratio
near 1 at real scale; `motion_report`: sharp turns only at contacts, no arc wobble or start-stops
inside a move; `staging_report` flags empty with shadow frames visible; `limb_extension`,
`rotation_flips`, `balance_report` as above; `roll_aliasing` ok. **Visual** (open every image): pose
strip, onion skin through the shot camera with tracks, `graph_image`, playblast frame sheets
(subject size, entry, shadow gap closing at contacts, spin readable), orbit views when the camera is
not locked.

## Common mistakes

| Mistake                                  | What it looks like                                                           | Fix                                                           |
| ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Whole blocking to Bezier                 | "floaty spaghetti"                                                           | `blocking_to_spline` with pillars, body only                  |
| Pillar on a continuous contact           | body brakes before impact                                                    | put that frame in `interpolate`; VECTOR on the foot           |
| AUTO handles on a hold                   | hold drifts past the pose                                                    | AUTO_CLAMPED; AUTO only for a settle                          |
| Heel curve eased during contact          | foot slides (5.8 cm per step measured)                                       | VECTOR or zero-length FREE handles                            |
| Jaw open on every syllable               | chattering mouth                                                             | big opens on `accent_frames` only                             |
| BOUNCE easing for a ball                 | no squash frame ever shows                                                   | `bouncing_ball` or keyed whole-frame contacts                 |
| Squash on a parent that also aims        | pattern twists on stretch frames (55 degrees measured on the old rig)        | `squash_modifier` (world axes) on the object itself           |
| Flights rounded to even frames           | hops lose or gain height, gravity changes per bounce (0.98 to 1.31 measured) | whole-frame contacts, odd flights allowed, one gravity        |
| Framing the whole set                    | subject 10% of frame, top 40% empty                                          | move in or shorten the travel until `staging_report` is clean |
| `display.light_direction` read as world  | shadow hidden behind the subject (0 px)                                      | `playblast_lighting(key_dir=...)`                             |
| Arcs checked in normalized camera coords | false sharp turns at apexes (aspect squeezes x)                              | `to_camera(..., res=(w, h))`                                  |
| Legs straight at stand or push-off       | IK stretch lengthens the leg (18% in the first jump draft)                   | soft knees, feet breakdown after take-off, VECTOR take-off    |

## Blender 5.2 notes

- `action.fcurves` is gone: channelbags via `bpy_extras.anim_utils` (`bx_anim.channelbag`).
  Assigning an action animates only if a slot matches; otherwise set `ad.action_slot`.
- One layer per action (`layers.new` raises); layer with the NLA plus an ADD or COMBINE action
  (`push_layer`).
- `keyframe_points.insert` gives BEZIER AUTO_CLAMPED; a Keyframe reference dies at the next insert
  on that curve.
- Headless: `anim.keyframe_insert` fails; `pose.breakdown` and `pose.blend_to_neighbor` need
  explicit `prev_frame`/`next_frame`; `render.opengl` refuses, so playblasts are Workbench renders.
- Workbench `scene.display.light_direction` is camera-relative; `matrix_world` is stale until
  `view_layer.update()`, so convert after it.
- GN modifier inputs key at `modifiers["X"].properties.inputs.Socket_n.value`.
- Playblast audio: sound strip plus `render.ffmpeg.audio_codec = 'AAC'`.
- Keymap: Up = previous key, Down = next (5.0). Not in 5.2: action layers, paste-pose blending,
  range world-space copy (5.3).

## References

- [`references/expert-notes.md`](references/expert-notes.md): principles, numbers and disagreements
  by expert, with timestamps; load when choosing between approaches or writing notes.
- [`references/procedures.md`](references/procedures.md): full tested code for every procedure
  (setup, blocking, spline, walk, lip sync, facial timing, contact pin, slots, layers, pose library,
  playblast, measurement, ball, staging, knee/flip/balance); load before writing code.
- [`references/critique.md`](references/critique.md): the review rubric per stage, staging
  thresholds and their calibration, how these animators phrase notes; load at every gate.
- [`references/sources.md`](references/sources.md): the 14 source videos, what each is best for,
  best timestamps.

# Blender blockout for a render-to-real video pass

The blockout is the guide clip: the video model copies the camera path, framing, lens feel, easing,
cut points, shot lengths, the position and scale of every mass, figure facing and every trajectory,
and it invents the rest from text and images (materials, light, weather, what each proxy really is,
faces, wardrobe, extras, sound). So the blockout has full authority over motion and layout and none
over look. Ambiguity ruins the pass; crudeness does not: a bent lamppost comes back as a snake,
loose limb blocks as extra people, an unmarked car driving backward. Fix identity in geometry first,
in prompt text second, and judge the result on a synced side-by-side of playblast and video, never
in the viewport alone. If a sibling skill named here is missing from your available skills, ask the
user to install it (`npx skills add scenario-labs/skills --skill <name>`); unattended, proceed from
tool schemas and flag the gap.

**REQUIRED BACKGROUND:** scenario-blender-expert (execution channel, review loop, 5.2 API changes).
Video generation: `scenario-blender` (the plugin's quote, generate and place flow), the `scenario`
skill (connection, uploads, jobs) and `scenario-seedance` (reference-video fields).

Toolkit: [`scripts/bx_blockout.py`](scripts/bx_blockout.py):
`import sys; sys.path.insert(0, "<this skill>/scripts"); [sys.modules.pop(m, None) for m in ("bx_blockout", "bx_kits")]; import bx_blockout as B`,
where `<this skill>` is the installed folder's absolute path. The pop drops a copy an earlier run
left in Blender's one Python. Builders are get-or-create by name, so a call can run again, and they
refuse a name the user's own work already holds (names are global to the file). An empty audit
result is a pass. The module docstring shows the call order.
[`scripts/bx_kits.py`](scripts/bx_kits.py) (`import bx_kits as K`, same rules) adds buildings,
stalls, trees, lamps, rocks and vehicles at three fidelity tiers, figures in four cast styles,
crowds, traffic, color schemes and `K.audit_budget`. Four worked scenes, simple to expert, with
render-pass results: [examples](references/examples.md) ([harness](scripts/examples/ex_common.py),
[1](scripts/examples/ex1_watchmaker.py), [2](scripts/examples/ex2_saltflat.py),
[3](scripts/examples/ex3_bridge.py), [4](scripts/examples/ex4_sky_islands.py)).

**Which skill.** This one: guides for a video model. Story previs and animatics judged by a director
and an editor: scenario-blender-previs-storyboard; an approved animatic that must guide a video
model is rebuilt here.

## 1. Restate the brief as a build plan

Before any call, write down:

- **Elements and their primitive**: "bus = long box with a marked front", "figures = colored
  capsules". Never model past what the brief names.
- **Dimensions** in meters for everything; when the brief is silent, take them from
  [the contract tables](references/contract.md) and say so.
- **Format**: integer fps, aspect, seconds. The range is 1 to fps x seconds (8 s at 24 fps: 1..192).
- **Shots**: count, move, lens, framing invariants ("hero always in frame, full figure"), cut style;
  beats pinned to seconds, converted to frames now.
- **Levels**: density (simple, medium, advanced, expert: footprint, elements, heroes, extras,
  shots), fidelity (rough, shaped, detailed) and color scheme, read off the brief and set apart:
  [levels](references/levels.md). Where the brief is silent (naming only heroes and shots is
  silent): advanced, shaped, category colors, and say so; drop to simple or medium only for one
  actor in one place. Expert means many elements, movers and cuts, never finer blocks.
- **Video model**, now: cast style and prompt grammar depend on it (`list_models` on the plugin
  lane, `recommend` on the hosted route).
- **Cast style** per character ([cast](references/cast.md)): a stand-in with limbs hands the model a
  gait to copy; one without limbs lets it invent body and motion. Default heroes to colored
  capsules, featured (two or three signature features: goggles, a hood, a held lantern) when
  characters must stay apart or carry the story's object; a rigged gray mannequin only when the
  blockout must own limb motion. Tell the user the style chosen, what it costs in control, and that
  the others can be A/B tested on a short window.
- **Identity colors**: hero red, then blue, green, yellow, purple, cyan.
- **Deliberate gaps** the video model fills, and **acceptance tests** the brief states: they become
  mandatory audits.

Decide what the brief leaves open and record the decision; do not stop to ask. Spending is the
exception: Scenario prices are shown and approved by the user (section 3). With a reference image:
list its masses, block them at plausible scale, match camera height and lens, `render_still` from
the camera, compare, adjust until the composition matches, and only then animate.

## 2. Output contract

Four deliverables: the scene, a locked camera timeline, the playblast, the hand-off sheet.

- **Scene hygiene.** Role prefixes (`ENV_`, `FIG_`, `PRP_`, `CAM_`, `CRV_`, `RIG_`, `NULL_target_`,
  full table in the contract), one root collection with role sub-collections. Park the default Cube,
  Light and Camera with `B.park`, never delete. If the file holds other work, build in a new scene
  (`B.make_scene`) and touch nothing existing; every object must trace to one of your stages.
- **Scale.** Meters, Z up, ground at z = 0, figure roots at the feet. The model keeps every mass
  where it is at its size, mistakes included. Nothing familiar for scale: add a `REF_` figure.
- **Color separates masses and names identities.** One saturated color per hero (`B.PALETTE`, hero
  red), the set in one `K.scheme` (category hues by default, identity grays, or material colors),
  extras in mid grays, one light, a dark world. `B.paint` and the kits set object color and
  materials; a kit carries several colors, so Solid view needs color type Material
  (`B.solid_view()`'s default and the playblast's). An all-gray playblast has lost identity. Recolor
  a kit through its arguments: its materials are shared per color. Grid or checker texture only
  where the camera travels and depth must read, declared "replace, never inherit" in the sheet.
- **Timeline.** `B.lock_format` before any geometry: integer fps, frames 1 to fps x seconds,
  1920x1080 (2520x1080 for 21:9) at 100 %. One camera per shot, bound to a `CUT_` marker on its
  first frame (`B.bind_cuts`), hard cuts, zero transition frames.
- **Camera rigs.** Rail: `B.rail_camera` (curve, dolly on Follow Path, aim with Track To, camera).
  Handheld tracking, straight push-in and multi-shot masters: recipes in the contract. Reframe by
  moving the aim target, never by rotating the camera.
- **Lens.** One lens per shot from shot size (`B.lens_for_coverage`; 28 mm orbits, 42 to 45 mm
  over-the-shoulder, 24 to 30 mm interiors, 85 mm macro), `clip_start` 0.05. A cut changes lens only
  by changing camera: never key a lens step on a cut frame. A lens may ease inside a shot (a
  deliberate zoom), never jump.
- **Easing.** Bezier keys with auto-clamped handles (`B.smooth_keys`); speed is key spacing on the
  rail (`B.key_rail`), a pause is two near-equal values. LINEAR only for per-frame baked travel
  (vehicles, wheels). Keys run past every cut so nothing stops on the boundary.
- **Handheld** is NOISE F-curve modifiers, never keyed jitter. Measure the result with
  `B.audit_handheld` against the budget in the contract; `animation_data_clear()` removes the
  modifiers, so re-add them after rekeying.

## 3. Channel: the Scenario Blender Plugin

The live channel is the plugin's local Scenario MCP server, `scenario-blender` (the guide at
[blender.scenario.com](https://blender.scenario.com/) calls the plugin Scenario for Blender). Tool
table, call limits and recovery after a timeout: [plugin](references/plugin.md). The two that bite
first: `execute_python` stays off until the user enables **Allow connected agents to run Python** (a
`PermissionError` means ask), and a call stops after 120 s, so send one stage piece per call and run
`B.stage_backup(label)` after each stage.

**Where the plugin's own tools fit** (details in [plugin](references/plugin.md)): its paid
**Blockout** (`estimate_blockout`, `approve_blockout`, then the user's **Build plan** button) suits
Stage 2 for a generic set and makes no figures, cameras or identity colors; **`camera_path`** keys
one camera around a static center for a single shot, never a tracking or multi-shot sequence (those
use `B.rail_camera`); **Render Video** is the video pass, section 6.

## 4. Build order

Back up after every stage; a reset is recovered from the last backup
([contract](references/contract.md)). Every `execute_python` call starts with
`B.guard(expected_file=..., scene=...)`: queued calls land in whatever file is open.

0. **Probe**, read-only: `scene_summary`, `datablocks_summary`. Other work present: new scene.
1. **Format and scaffolding**: `B.make_scene`, `B.lock_format`, `B.collection` tree, `B.park`, dark
   world.
2. **Set**: kits at the chosen fidelity (`K.building`, `K.stall`, `K.tree`) or thick boxes (`B.box`)
   at true scale, repeats as linked duplicates (`K.instance`). Or the plugin Blockout for a generic
   set.
3. **Figures**: `K.figure(..., style=, features=)` per hero in the chosen cast style, root at the
   feet, facing along travel ([cast](references/cast.md)). Travel with `K.walk_path` from a table of
   (frame, position), stride 0.42 x height for a walk, about 0.7 for a run; gestures with `K.pose`;
   extras with `K.crowd(style=...)`.
4. **Props and vehicles**: literal primitives at true position. Mark a vehicle's front in geometry
   (light blocks and grille in front, dark red at the rear); wheels at z = radius, separate with one
   spin channel only when a close shot reads rotation (kit wheels are body mesh). No loose blocks
   near a figure.
5. **Light**: one area light; named key, fill, rim only when the brief designs light.
6. **Cameras**: rigs and lenses per shot, `B.bind_cuts`.
7. **Motion polish**: `B.key_rail` and `B.smooth_keys`, keys past cuts, handheld, vehicle travel as
   one monotone curve keyed per frame.
8. **Audit** (section 5) until clean. When set dressing hides the hero, move the blockers and keep
   the camera plan.
9. **Finalize**: frame 1, shot 1's camera, `B.audit_frames`, `B.state_audit`, final backup, then
   playblast and hand-off sheet.

## 5. Audits: numbers judge, then look

| Check                                | Helper                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Frame math and resolution            | `B.audit_frames(seconds, fps)`                                                |
| Markers bound, switches, lens, jumps | `B.audit_cuts()` (`same_lens_across_cuts=True` when the brief wants one lens) |
| Subjects in frame per shot           | `B.audit_framing({"CAM_s1": ["FIG_red"]}, whole=True)` for full figures       |
| Head never hidden                    | `B.audit_occlusion("FIG_red")`                                                |
| Too close, outside the legal volume  | `B.audit_distance(subject, volume=...)` (full-figure shots only)              |
| Interpenetration                     | `B.audit_intersections(names)`                                                |
| Feet and wheels on the ground        | `B.audit_ground(names)`                                                       |
| Handheld amplitude                   | `B.audit_handheld("CAM_s1")`                                                  |
| Census before hand-off               | `B.state_audit()`                                                             |

Audit each shot's own subject (the wheel for a macro, the hand for an insert). Then look:
`set_frame` and `render_still` at the first, middle and last frame of every shot, and check what
numbers miss: a vehicle's front, connected figures, rigid props without organic curves, nothing
stray at frame edges, an ending as locked as the opening. Thresholds and readings:
[audits](references/audits.md). An audit samples every `step` frames; on a long shot raise `step` to
stay under the call limit.

## 6. Playblast, hand-off sheet, video pass

**Playblast.** Headless, on the latest `B.stage_backup` copy, with scenario-blender-expert's
`bx_review.playblast(out_path, res_pct=100)`: an H.264 MP4 of the scene camera over the frame range
in Workbench, cuts following the bound markers. Use the session's binary (`bpy.app.binary_path`): an
older `blender` on PATH refuses the file. With no shell, the same call through `execute_python`
blocks Blender while it renders: keep it to short clips, and after a timeout look for the file
before running it again. Add camera stills at each shot's start, middle and end.

**Hand-off sheet**, built from the scene ([template](references/handoff.md)): color legend tied to
reference images, `K.cast()` rows, the cut list from `B.cut_list()` with exact times, which entities
are blocked and which exist only in words, every artifact with its timecode, each motion state in
words ("creeps", "stands still"), and tie-break clauses ("if text and video disagree about motion,
the video wins").

**Video pass**, always through Scenario, after the user approves the exact price. Unattended, stop
at the quote (`estimate_cost` or `dry_run`), report it, and skip local uploads that need the user's
file choice:

- **Plugin, Render Video lane**: `B.solid_view()` so the capture shows identity colors,
  `force_solid` false (it turns everything one gray), a timeline length the model accepts, then
  `list_models`, `model_schema`, `render_form` (`configure` with `parameters`
  `{"duration": <clip seconds>}`, `prepare`, `inspect`), `estimate_cost`, `generate`, `wait_for_job`
  and the result application, step by step in [handoff](references/handoff.md) Route 1. The capture
  is a silent 1280x720 clip.
- **Hosted Scenario MCP**, for the full-resolution playblast: upload the playblast as the `scenario`
  skill shows, discover a model that takes a reference video, `model_schema_get`, `model_run` with
  `dry_run` first, `jobs_wait`, `asset_download`.

Write the prompt motion-first: the clip is rehearsal footage, the cast is described by role and
motion, never by the proxies' shapes, and style comes from a four-panel style board rather than one
restyled frame. A capsule cast adds a stand-in clause (the capsules only mark position, height, pace
and heading) and a gait clause ([cast](references/cast.md)). On the plugin lane the plugin states
the clip's and images' roles itself, so `look` holds only cast and style. Grammar, clauses and
tested limits: [handoff](references/handoff.md).

## Worked example

Brief: "10 s, 24 fps: a red runner sprints between crate rows toward camera in a warehouse; a blue
guard steps out at second 6; handheld 35 mm backing away."

1. `scene_summary` `{"fields": ["type"], "limit": 100}`: the file holds other work, so build beside
   it.
2. `execute_python`: `B.make_scene("BLK_warehouse")`; next call `B.guard(scene="BLK_warehouse")`,
   `B.lock_format(24, 10)` (1..240), collections, backup.
3. Floor 34 x 20 m, 7 m walls, two rows of 1.2 m crates with `B.box`; backup.
4. `K.figure("red", 1.8, (0, 15, 0), style="featured", features=("hood",))`, then `K.walk_path` to
   (0, 1) by frame 200 with a sprint's stride (1.3 m); the blue guard, a capsule, steps into the
   aisle over frames 144 to 156; backup.
5. `B.rail_camera("s1", [(0, 3, 1.5), (0, -1, 1.5), (0, -4, 1.5)], follow="FIG_red", target_offset=(0, 0, 1.2), lens=35)`,
   `B.key_rail("RIG_dolly_s1", [(1, 0), (260, 1)])`, `B.bind_cuts([(1, "CAM_s1")])`, handheld noise
   within budget.
6. `B.audit_frames(10, 24)`, `B.audit_cuts()`,
   `B.audit_framing({"CAM_s1": ["FIG_red", "FIG_blue"]}, whole=True)`,
   `B.audit_occlusion("FIG_red")`, `B.audit_handheld("CAM_s1")`; move crates until clean.
7. `set_frame` 1, 120, 240 with `render_still` each, and look. Backup, headless playblast,
   `B.cut_list()` into the sheet.

## Common mistakes and downstream misreads

- **Identity not in geometry**: a floating head or slab arms; loose blocks near a figure read as
  extra people; a car with no marked front driven in reverse; an occupant behind an opaque cabin
  vanishes (give the cabin alpha).
- **Camera grammar**: a key on the cut frame freezes motion there; an overhead orbit read as a cut;
  seats mirrored on a reverse camera; invented reverse shots in dialogue; drift in the last seconds.
- **Ambiguous motion**: slow proxy motion reads as either rolling or still; the sheet decides.
- **Copied limbs**: on a reference-video model, stepped or looped legs come back stiff, in lockstep
  or sliding; switch that character to a capsule ([cast](references/cast.md)).
- **Fragile detail**: sub-pixel parts change identity between restyles; a style that implies text
  invents gibberish lettering.
- **Opening-frame fiction**: "starts at the door" needs a doorway behind frame 1; high shots over
  flat ground read flat.
- **State drift**: render probes that leave resolution or file path changed; pre-existing objects
  adopted as your own; Blender 5 slotted actions hiding F-curves (use `B.fcurves`).

# Blender expert (router and agent protocol)

Expert-level Blender work is a loop, not a script: build big to small, and at every stage turn the
model, measure it and fix it before adding detail. This skill is the protocol every Blender task
follows and the map to the domain skills distilled from Blender Studio artists, Blender Conference
talks and top instructors (sources in each skill). If a sibling skill named here is missing from
your available skills, ask the user to install it
(`npx skills add scenario-labs/skills --skill <name>`); unattended, proceed from tool schemas and
flag the gap.

## 1. Execution channel

- **Live GUI Blender** (user's session over the MCP bridge), for anything interactive: real
  sculpt/paint brushes, weight painting, viewport screenshots. One short, idempotent script per call
  returning a compact result dict. Get-or-create by name. Never touch objects you did not create.
  Save a stage backup `bpy.ops.wm.save_as_mainfile(filepath=..., copy=True)` after each stage.
- **Headless helper** `blender -b [file] --factory-startup --python-exit-code 1 -P x.py -- args`,
  for renders, audits, batch ops, anything when no bridge is up. Use `--factory-startup` so the
  user's add-ons and preferences stay out of the run (an add-on can call the network or change
  defaults); the Scenario Blender Plugin's headless server,
  `blender --background scene.blend --command scenario_blender`, is the exception because it needs
  the extension loaded. Without `--python-exit-code` a failing script still exits 0. Print a final
  machine-readable result line.

Never open your own GUI Blender window to test things on the user's machine: windows steal focus and
pile up. Live work goes through the user's already-running Blender; everything else runs headless,
one Blender process at a time per agent (other sessions may be rendering on the same machine).

**Live channel: the Scenario Blender Plugin.** When the user's Blender runs the Scenario Blender
Plugin, its local MCP server `scenario-blender` is the bridge. Setup, quotes, generation and placing
results are the `scenario-blender` skill's work; this section covers the bpy side (guide at
[blender.scenario.com](https://blender.scenario.com/)). Its tool names differ from other Blender MCP
servers: there is no `execute_blender_code`, `get_scene_info`, `get_viewport_screenshot` or
`import_asset`.

| Step                          | Plugin tool and main arguments                                                                                                                 |
| ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Read the scene before acting  | `scene_summary`, then `object_detail` with `name` for one object and `datablocks_summary` for counts                                           |
| Check an API before scripting | `blender_api_help` with `path`, such as `bpy.types.BevelModifier`                                                                              |
| Run bpy                       | `execute_python` with `code`; `bpy` and `result = {}` are preloaded, so fill `result`                                                          |
| Look                          | `screenshot_viewport` (viewport with overlays), `render_still` with `source` (`CAMERA` or `VIEWPORT`), `width` and `height`; both need the GUI |
| Select, move the timeline     | `select_objects` with `names` (a list), `set_frame` with `frame`                                                                               |

Read each tool's input schema from the server before its first call: it is the reference for
optional arguments.

- `execute_python` stays off until the user enables **Allow connected agents to run Python** in the
  plugin preferences. A `PermissionError` means ask for it or stay on the specific tools. A refused
  spelling (quit, factory reset, file deletion) changed nothing: rewrite the call.
- Budget every call: the plugin stops a call after 120 s and some agent clients stop waiting after
  60 s. Make one logical change per call, so one Undo reverts it, and send bakes, QuadriFlow on
  dense meshes, turntables, playblasts and final renders to a headless Blender working on a saved
  copy.
- A timed-out call has an unknown outcome: read the scene again before retrying, never resend it
  blindly.
- The plugin's tools never save the user's own file. The live channel's stage backup
  (`save_as_mainfile(..., copy=True)` through `execute_python`) writes a separate file and leaves
  the open file and its unsaved state alone: it is also the saved copy that headless work starts
  from. Ask the user to save their own file at milestones; with no one to ask, keep working from the
  copies and say in the report that the open file is still unsaved.

Check `bpy.app.version` first; this skill set targets 5.2 LTS, while the Scenario Blender Plugin
also runs on 5.0 and 5.1 (`scene_summary` reports the version), so check the version timeline in the
deltas before using a recent API. Many tutorials the experts recorded use 2.8x to 4.2 UI: read
[`references/blender-5.2-deltas.md`](references/blender-5.2-deltas.md) before trusting any
remembered operator, brush name or API.

**Verified capability matrix (Blender 5.2.1):**

| Action                                                                                                                                | Headless                                               | GUI session                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------- |
| Voxel remesh, QuadriFlow, multires subdivide, modifiers, bmesh, UV ops with edit-mode context, Cycles/EEVEE/Workbench renders, baking | yes                                                    | yes                                               |
| `bpy.ops.brush.asset_activate`, dyntopo toggle                                                                                        | yes                                                    | yes                                               |
| Brush strokes (`sculpt.brush_stroke`, `paint.image_paint`, `paint.weight_paint`)                                                      | no (poll fails)                                        | yes, via [`scripts/bx_gui.py`](scripts/bx_gui.py) |
| `paint.mask_flood_fill`, `sculpt.mesh_filter`                                                                                         | CRASHES Blender                                        | yes, via `bx_gui.run()`                           |
| Programmatic sculpting on mesh data                                                                                                   | yes, `scenario-blender-sculpting/scripts/bx_sculpt.py` | yes                                               |

## 2. The expert loop (every domain)

1. **Establish the brief** in numbers: purpose (film, game engine, still, animation), budgets (tris,
   texture size, frame range), style (stylized or realistic), references. When the brief is silent,
   choose a documented default from the domain skill and write it down.
2. **Plan the stages** the domain skill defines. Never start with detail.
3. **Build one stage** with the smallest scripts that do it.
4. **Gate the stage:** run the measurable checks ([`scripts/bx_audit.py`](scripts/bx_audit.py) for
   meshes, the domain's own checks) AND render a review sheet
   ([`scripts/bx_review.py`](scripts/bx_review.py): silhouette, matcap, wire from
   front/side/three-quarter/low) and open it with the image reader. Experts orbit constantly; the
   review sheet is the agent's orbit. Every image read stays in the agent's context: for quick looks
   use `render_still` at about 768 px wide or `screenshot_viewport`, and keep review sheets near
   1600 px (`res=400` for four views and three modes). Judge with the domain's
   `references/critique.md`.
5. **Fix before advancing.** A problem found at blockout costs one script; found after texturing it
   costs the stage.
6. **Deliver with evidence:** run the delivery gate (`bx_audit.deliverable`, below) on the parts of
   the asset before any export or handoff and fix every error. Then report final renders, gate and
   audit numbers, and what was not verified.

Never report a model, rig, animation or render as done without having looked at a render of it.

## 3. Persona pipelines

| Persona / brief                                     | Skill chain                                                                                                                                                                                                | Deliverable                                                  |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Character artist, stylized or realistic             | scenario-blender-sculpting, scenario-blender-retopology, scenario-blender-uv-baking, scenario-blender-texturing-shading, scenario-blender-hair                                                             | sculpt, animation-ready low poly, UVs, baked maps, materials |
| AI-mesh finisher (Scenario 3D output to production) | gate the generated asset, scenario-blender-retopology (or cleanup + remesh), scenario-blender-uv-baking (bake FROM the generated high), scenario-blender-texturing-shading; generation itself: scenario-3d | clean, UV'd, baked asset at a stated budget                  |
| Game asset artist                                   | scenario-blender-hard-surface or scenario-blender-sculpting, scenario-blender-retopology (game budget), scenario-blender-uv-baking, scenario-blender-texturing-shading, scenario-blender-export            | low poly + PBR set, exported glTF/FBX                        |
| Rigger / character TD                               | scenario-blender-rigging                                                                                                                                                                                   | rig with controls, weights, deformation tests                |
| Animator                                            | scenario-blender-previs-storyboard (shot planning), scenario-blender-animation                                                                                                                             | blocked, splined, polished shot + playblast                  |
| Story / previs artist                               | scenario-blender-previs-storyboard, scenario-blender-grease-pencil                                                                                                                                         | shots, cameras, animatic                                     |
| Look-dev and lighting artist                        | scenario-blender-texturing-shading, scenario-blender-lighting-rendering                                                                                                                                    | lit, color-managed, composited renders                       |
| Technical artist / procedural                       | scenario-blender-geometry-nodes                                                                                                                                                                            | node-group assets, procedural systems                        |
| 2D / 2.5D animator                                  | scenario-blender-grease-pencil                                                                                                                                                                             | GP animation                                                 |

Related skills outside this set: scenario-3d (generate meshes to finish here), scenario-textures (AI
textures).

## 4. Shared toolkit (`scripts/`, all tested on 5.2.1)

- `bx_audit.py`: `audit(obj, high=None)` returns quads %, n-gons, poles (valence 3 / 5+ / 6+),
  non-manifold, loose, duplicates, flipped faces, self-intersections, boundary loops, symmetry %,
  edge-length CV, and fidelity to a high poly; `verdict(report)` lists problems. CLI:
  `blender -b f.blend --python bx_audit.py -- --object Name [--high Sculpt] [--json out.json]`.
- `bx_audit.deliverable(objs, profile="game")`: the delivery gate. `audit` grades topology; this
  grades what an engine, renderer or slicer receives, across the parts of ONE asset:
  - errors in every profile: floating parts and fragments, closed parts inside out, negative scale;
    z-fighting between parts everywhere but `print`;
  - by profile (`game`, `render`, `print`, `roblox`): unapplied scale, faces pointing into a part
    (an error from 0.1% of its surface, a warning below except for `print`), duplicate faces, no UV
    map under an image texture, open borders for `print` and `roblox`, any gap between parts for
    `print`, the Roblox 20,000-triangle mesh limit (checked 2026-10-18).
  - Returns `{pass, errors, warnings, per_object}`. Tolerances scale with the asset's diagonal.
    UV-seam splits from a glTF import are welded for the checks, so seams never read as holes.
  - Gate separate props one by one: every prop but the largest reads as floating.
  - CLI, exit code 2 on failure:
    `blender -b --factory-startup --python-exit-code 1 -P bx_audit.py -- --deliverable [--import model.glb | --objects A B] --profile game [--json out.json]`.
  - Fixes: apply scale (`obj.data.transform(Matrix.Diagonal(obj.scale).to_4x4())`, then
    `obj.scale = (1, 1, 1)`; a scale the message puts on a parent: select the parent and its
    children, `bpy.ops.object.transform_apply(scale=True)`), `bmesh.ops.recalc_face_normals` for
    inside-out parts, `bmesh.ops.reverse_faces` for faces pointing inward
    (`per_object[name]["inward_faces_at"]`), delete or offset the hidden face of a z-fighting pair,
    join or move floating parts, delete fragments.
  - Engines cull back faces: to see what they draw, render Workbench with
    `scene.display.shading.show_backface_culling = True` and compare with it off.
- `bx_review.py`: `review(objs, out_dir, views, modes)` writes one contact sheet (rows = modes, cols
  = views) in a temporary scene, user settings untouched; `playblast(out_path, res_pct=50)`;
  `turntable(obj, out_path, frames=72, res=720)`. Only `review` has a command line: call the others
  from a short wrapper script.
- `bx_gui.py`: real brushes in a live session: `set_view`, `activate_brush(mode, name)`,
  `stroke(mode, world_points, size, strength)`, `run(op, **kw)`, `set_paint_color`, `screenshot`.

Import pattern: `import sys; sys.path.append("<this skill>/scripts"); import bx_audit, bx_review`.
Replace `<this skill>` with the absolute path of the installed skill folder: Blender's Python does
not share the agent's working directory, and over a live bridge the code runs inside the user's
Blender. Check the path in the first call (`result["ok"] = os.path.isdir(path)`) and
`importlib.reload` a module after the skill updates.

## 5. Version traps that break most remembered code

- Brushes are assets (4.3):
  `bpy.ops.brush.asset_activate(asset_library_type='ESSENTIALS', asset_library_identifier="", relative_asset_identifier="brushes/essentials_brushes-mesh_sculpt.blend/Brush/Clay Strips")`;
  brush size is a diameter (5.0); Flatten/Fill/Scrape merged into the Plane type.
- Auto Smooth removed (4.1): `mesh.shade_smooth()` / Smooth by Angle modifier; voxel remesh output
  is flat-shaded until you call `shade_smooth()`.
- Principled BSDF v2 (4.0): address sockets by name; Emission strength defaults to 0.
- `BLENDER_EEVEE` is the EEVEE Next identifier in 5.x (`BLENDER_EEVEE_NEXT` fails).
- Compositor is a node group (5.0): `scene.compositing_node_group`, not `scene.node_tree`.
- Video output: set `image_settings.media_type = 'VIDEO'` before `file_format = 'FFMPEG'` (5.0).
- Slotted actions (4.4), `action.fcurves` removed (5.0): use
  `bpy_extras.anim_utils.action_get_channelbag_for_slot(action, slot)`.
- Bone collections replace armature layers (4.0); Grease Pencil v3 is `GREASEPENCIL` with
  `bpy.ops.grease_pencil.*` (4.3).
- Positional context dicts for operators are gone: `with bpy.context.temp_override(...)`.
- `obj.matrix_world` is stale right after setting location/scale until `view_layer.update()`.

## References

- [`references/bpy-reliability.md`](references/bpy-reliability.md): checklist and tested procedures
  for reliable bpy (operators vs data API, stale references, evaluated vs original data, idempotent
  headless jobs, numpy bulk access, node trees, persistence). Load before writing any non-trivial
  script.
- `references/blender-5.2-deltas.md`: full, cited list of what changed from 2.8x to 5.2 per domain
  (load before writing code from memory or following an old tutorial).

# Blender export (engine-ready files)

An export is done when the file has been re-imported and measured, not when the exporter returned
`FINISHED`. Gate the asset first, export with a preset, then round-trip the file. This skill builds
on `scenario-blender-expert` (execution channels, the delivery gate) and imports its scripts, so
install the two side by side. If a sibling skill named here is missing from your available skills,
ask the user to install it (`npx skills add scenario-labs/skills --skill <name>`); unattended,
proceed from tool schemas and flag the gap.

Toolkit: [`scripts/bx_export.py`](scripts/bx_export.py). Per-engine facts with their sources:
[`references/engines.md`](references/engines.md).

## Quick reference

| Target                   | Preset            | File                | Engine side                                |
| ------------------------ | ----------------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| Unity, static mesh       | `unity`           | FBX                 | import defaults                            |
| Unity, character         | `unity_skeletal`  | FBX                 | leave Bake Axis Conversion off             |
| Unreal Engine            | `unreal`          | FBX                 | Convert Scene Unit (to centimeters)        |
| Unreal Engine, character | `unreal_skeletal` | FBX                 | one root bone                              |
| Godot 4                  | `godot`           | GLB                 | import defaults; Generate LODs in the dock |
| Roblox                   | `roblox`          | FBX                 | 20,000 triangles per mesh                  |
| three.js and the web     | `web`             | GLB, meshopt, WebP  | `MeshoptDecoder`; not for Godot            |
| any glTF reader          | `gltf`            | GLB                 |                                            |
| USD pipelines            | `usd`             | USDC                |                                            |
| Apple AR Quick Look      | `usdz`            | USDZ, 2048 textures |                                            |
| 3D printing              | `print`           | STL in millimeters  | slicer reads millimeters                   |

The Unity and Godot presets were imported into Unity 6000.3 and Godot 4.7.2 and measured; `unreal`,
`unreal_skeletal` and `roblox` follow Epic's and Roblox's documentation and pass the Blender round
trip only. The measurements live in [`references/engines.md`](references/engines.md).

## Procedure

1. **Gate.** Run `bx_audit.deliverable(parts, profile)` from `scenario-blender-expert` and fix every
   error. Scale left on an object travels into the engine as the node's transform.
2. **Pick the preset** from the table. Pass every object the file needs: a skinned mesh AND its
   armature, LOD meshes and their group, collision meshes beside their render mesh.
3. **Export:** `bxe.export(path, preset, objects, **overrides)`. Any exporter keyword overrides the
   preset, such as `bake_anim=True` on `roblox` for an animated file. The result records the
   settings used.
4. **Round-trip:** `bxe.round_trip(path, objects, preset=...)` re-imports the file in a background
   Blender, leaving the open scene alone. It compares size (1 mm), triangles, deforming bones, root
   bones (one expected), armature scale, shape keys and every action stored for the objects, by
   name. Then it lists every difference. Fix each one, or say why it is expected.
5. **glTF contents:** `bxe.glb_summary(path)` lists `extensions_required`, morph targets, skins,
   clips and image types without Blender. A loader refuses a file that requires an extension it
   lacks.
6. **Engine check:** import into the engine and look, with `scenario-unity-pipeline-automation`,
   `scenario-unreal-pipeline-automation` or `scenario-godot-pipeline-automation`.

## Scale, axes and units

- Blender works in meters, Z-up, with the asset's front facing -Y. glTF is meters, Y-up
  (`export_yup`). FBX stores its axes as metadata; the presets write -Z forward, Y up.
- Keep `scene.unit_settings.scale_length` at 1.0. Any other value rescales every export.
- Apply object scale before export: `obj.data.transform(Matrix.Diagonal(obj.scale).to_4x4())`, then
  `obj.scale = (1, 1, 1)`, so the engine node imports at scale 1.
- FBX scale: `unity` writes `FBX_SCALE_ALL` (Unity reads file scale 1). `unreal` keeps
  `FBX_SCALE_NONE` (Unity reads it as file scale 0.01, a centimeter file). `roblox` uses
  `FBX_SCALE_UNITS`, as Roblox's export requirements ask.
- STL has no unit and slicers read millimeters, so `print` multiplies by 1000.

## Characters

- Export the armature with its meshes. `use_armature_deform_only` leaves control bones out, so keep
  every deforming bone in one hierarchy under one root bone. Unreal's importer reports "Found
  multiple roots. The importer only supports one root per mesh."
- `add_leaf_bones` is off in every preset. Left on, each chain gains an extra end bone that breaks
  retargeting.
- `unity_skeletal` and `unreal_skeletal` bake every action (`bake_anim_use_all_actions`), one clip
  per action. Unity names each clip `Armature|Action` (measured: `Rig|Wave`), so name actions as the
  clips should read. glTF exports each action as an animation under its own name.
- `roblox` exports no animation. For an animated file, pass `bake_anim=True` to `export()` and to
  `round_trip()`, which then compares the actions too.
- Shape keys travel in FBX (blend shapes), glTF (morph targets, names in `extras.targetNames`) and
  USD. Building ARKit or viseme sets is `scenario-blender-rigging`'s work.
- Roblox: at most 4 influences per vertex, bones frozen (scale 1, rotation 0), root at the origin
  with no influences, one animation track per mesh. Check influences with
  `max(len(v.groups) for v in obj.data.vertices)`.

## LODs and collision

- `bxe.lods(obj, ratios=(0.5, 0.25))` renames the mesh `Name_LOD0` and adds decimated `Name_LOD1..n`
  under an empty called `Name`, which takes the mesh's place under its parent. Static meshes only:
  it refuses a skinned mesh. Unity builds the LOD Group from those names. Godot generates LODs at
  import (Generate LODs). Unreal documents "Import LODs", all LODs sharing one pivot. The group
  exports as a plain FBX Null, and Unreal's import of it is unmeasured.
- `bxe.collision(obj, engine, shape)` adds a collision mesh named for the importer:
  - Unreal: `UCX_Name_00` (convex hull) or `UBX_Name_00` (box), exported in the same FBX.
  - Godot: `Name-convcolonly` for `convex` (one hull) and `box` (the bounds, a box collider), or
    `Name-colonly` for `mesh` (the mesh as a trimesh, static bodies only).
  - Unity and Roblox: returns None. Colliders are set in the editor.
- Decimation can wreck UV seams and silhouettes. Review every LOD with `bx_review` before export.

## Batch conversion

```bash
blender -b --factory-startup --python-exit-code 1 -P bx_export.py -- \
        --batch /abs/in /abs/out --preset godot --profile game
```

For every model in the folder (GLB, glTF, FBX, OBJ, USD, STL, PLY): import into an empty scene, run
the delivery gate, export with the preset, re-import and compare. It writes `/abs/out/report.json`
with each file's gate errors, size and round-trip differences. One failing file never stops the
folder: it gets a `failed` entry. Two inputs sharing a name keep their format in the output name
(`hero_fbx.glb`, `hero_glb.glb`). Open the report before calling the batch done.

## Worked example: a generated GLB to Unity and Godot

```python
import sys
sys.path.append("/abs/skills/scenario-blender-expert/scripts")
sys.path.append("/abs/skills/scenario-blender-export/scripts")
import bpy, bx_audit, bx_export as bxe

bpy.ops.wm.read_factory_settings(use_empty=True)
bpy.ops.import_scene.gltf(filepath="/abs/in/robot.glb")
parts = [o.name for o in bpy.context.scene.objects if o.type == "MESH"]
gate = bx_audit.deliverable(parts, profile="game")
print(gate["errors"])            # fix each one, then gate again until "pass" is True

bxe.export("/abs/out/robot.fbx", "unity", parts)
print(bxe.round_trip("/abs/out/robot.fbx", parts, preset="unity")["diffs"])   # []
bxe.export("/abs/out/robot.glb", "godot", parts)
print(bxe.glb_summary("/abs/out/robot.glb")["extensions_required"])            # []
```

A generated GLB often holds one object per part, all sharing the asset's pivot. Keep them as
separate objects when the engine should animate or swap parts. Join them (`bpy.ops.object.join` with
the parts selected) for a single static prop, then gate again.

## Common mistakes

- Calling an export done on `FINISHED`. The exporter succeeds on files the engine imports at 100x
  scale or without the skin.
- Exporting a skinned mesh without its armature, or the armature without its mesh.
- Setting Bake Axis Conversion or Apply Transform to remove the armature node's rotation: neither
  removes it, and the first turns the character around.
- The `web` preset for Godot, or any compressed GLB for a loader without its decoder. Check
  `extensions_required` first.
- FBX textures left as external paths: the presets copy and embed them (`path_mode="COPY"`,
  `embed_textures=True`), so the file travels alone. `export()` gives packed images without an
  extension (as a GLB import leaves them) a `.jpg` or `.png` name first. An image never saved (a new
  bake target) or edited since travels as a packed copy of its pixels (`packed_unsaved_images`).
- A textured FBX that shows untextured in Unity: the default import keeps embedded textures inside
  the file. Extract Textures (Materials tab) into the model's folder assigns them.
- An STL at Blender scale: a 10 cm part prints at 0.1 mm.
- LODs exported without a look: decimation can collapse thin parts.
